# STEP 2 — THE STRUCTURE

---

## A. WHERE WOULD THE CI GUARD LIVE?

### A.1 The complete verification surface (11 workflows, exhaustive)

| Workflow | Trigger | What it validates | Network egress | Cadence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | `push: main` (paths-ignore changelog), `workflow_dispatch` | Builds `android` target, runs `container-structure-test test/android.yml` | Yes (`egress-policy: audit`, Docker Hub login, full apt/network build) | Post-merge |
| `build.yml` | `pull_request` (**no path filter**), `workflow_dispatch` | 8 jobs — see A.2 | Yes (audit) | Every PR |
| `windows.yml` | `pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch` | Calls `windows-image.yml` with `push: false` | (no harden-runner step at all) | Every PR |
| `windows-image.yml` | `workflow_call` only | Windows image build/test | Yes | Called |
| `gx.yml` | `pull_request` **paths-filtered** to `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**`, `.github/gx.toml`, `.github/gx.lock`; `workflow_dispatch` | `gx lint` (jobs `lint`, `tidy`) | Yes — needs `GITHUB_TOKEN`, resolves SHAs against api.github.com | Every matching PR |
| `update-docs.yml` | `pull_request` **paths-filtered** to `docs/build.mjs`, `docs/examples.cue`, `config/version.json` | `mise run docs` then `git diff --exit-code` | Yes (audit) | Every matching PR |
| `update-version.yml` | `schedule: 0 0 * * MON-FRI`, `workflow_dispatch` | Flutter/Android/Windows version derivation + PR | Yes | Weekday cron |
| `scorecard.yml` | `schedule: 15 11 * * 2`, `push` | OSSF Scorecard | Yes | Weekly cron |
| `release.yml` | `push` (tags), `workflow_dispatch` | Publish + `script/verify_published_image.sh` | Yes | On tag |
| `prepare-release.yml` | `push` paths-filtered, `workflow_dispatch` | Tag creation | Yes | On merge |
| `cleanup-pr-image.yml` | `pull_request` (closed) | GHCR tag cleanup | Yes | PR close |

### A.2 `build.yml` is the de-facto meta lane — and it already has the right shape

`.github/workflows/build.yml:372-445` contains **three pure-config, no-image, ~10-second jobs** that are structurally identical to what the deb guard needs:

- `validate-version-files` (`build.yml:372-390`) — `cue vet config/schema.cue -d '#Version' config/version.json`
- `validate-generated-config` (`build.yml:392-414`) — runs `script/update_test.sh`, then `git add -A && git diff --exit-code HEAD`
- `build-docs` (`build.yml:416-444`) — `mise run docs` + artifact upload

All three: `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`, harden-runner + checkout + mise-action, **no `needs:`**, no image build, no matrix, no secrets. `build.yml` has **no `paths:` filter** (`build.yml:4-5`), so these run on every PR unconditionally. A `validate-renovate-config` job appended here would be the fourth sibling in an established pattern, not an orphan workflow.

The `git diff --exit-code` idiom in `validate-generated-config:412-414` and `update-docs.yml:49-57` is the repo's **existing "regenerate and compare" verification primitive**, used twice already.

### A.3 `script/renovate_validate.sh` is invoked by NOTHING

```
script/renovate_validate.sh:1
npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator --strict
```

Exhaustive grep across all workflows, `mise.toml`, all scripts, and `package.json`-equivalents: **zero call sites**. The only three references in the repo are prose in archived openspec docs:
- `openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/design.md:5`
- `openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/design.md:48`
- `openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/tasks.md:4` ("- [x] 1.2 Run `script/renovate_validate.sh`…")

It is a **manual, human-invoked script recorded as a checklist item in a change document**. PR #531's `tasks.md:23` does the same thing again ("- [x] 4.2 Run `script/renovate_validate.sh`"). This is the single most important structural finding in part A: the repo's only Renovate verification is a script a human is trusted to remember to run, whose evidence lives in a markdown checkbox. It is not a CI check, it is not in `mise.toml`, and it has no `paths:` trigger. `.github/renovate.json` is the **only significant config file in the repo with zero automated verification** — `config/version.json` has `cue vet` + `update_test.sh` + `mise run docs`, `.github/gx.toml` has `gx lint` + `gx tidy`, workflows have `gx lint`. Renovate config has a script nobody calls.

### A.4 Nothing runs a Renovate dry-run anywhere

`npx renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup` appears only in PR #531's `tasks.md:24` and `design.md:78` as a **locally-executed, manually-transcribed** verification. Its output was pasted into `design.md:80-87` as prose. No workflow has ever invoked `renovate` as a binary.

### A.5 gx is NOT the natural home

The memory "Workflow lint belongs in gx" holds within its actual domain, and that domain is narrow. From the installed binary (`gx 0.7.2 --help`):

> `CLI to manage Github Actions dependencies` — commands: `tidy`, `init`, `upgrade`, `lint`

`gx lint --help` enumerates every rule it has:
> action-hygiene: `sha-mismatch`, `unpinned`, `stale-comment`, `unsynced-manifest`
> workflow-security: `missing-permissions`, `excessive-permissions`, `dangerous-trigger`, `pr-head-checkout`, `missing-concurrency`, `unprotected-secrets`

Ten rules, all about `uses:` references and workflow YAML security. **gx has no concept of Dockerfiles, Renovate config, apt, deb, or datasources.** Its input surface is `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**`, `.github/gx.toml`, `.github/gx.lock` — exactly the `gx.yml:5-9` paths filter. Its network egress is api.github.com for SHA resolution, not deb.debian.org.

Reinforcing that this boundary is deliberate and already reasoned: `openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/proposal.md:19` explicitly says the existing Renovate coverage in `actions-version-tracking` "is about GitHub Actions via gx.toml — a separate manager and datasource. No existing spec covers the image's apt pins."

Adding deb-pin resolution to gx would mean teaching a GitHub-Actions dependency manager to parse Dockerfiles and query Debian mirrors. That is a different product. **gx is the right home for the "workflow lint" boundary and the wrong home for this one.**

### A.6 So: where does it land?

There is a real `validate-*` lane in `build.yml:372-414` and the guard fits its shape exactly. But note the mismatch that makes it not-quite-a-fit: every existing job in that lane is **hermetic** — `cue vet`, `cue export`, `node docs/build.mjs` all read only committed files. The proposed guard would be the **first job in the repo whose pass/fail depends on the state of a third-party server at the moment it runs**. That is a new property for this lane, not a new file.

---

## B. WHAT SITS BETWEEN THE PARTS?

### B.1 The chain, with the seam inventory

```
SEAM 1  android.Dockerfile:143  # renovate: depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless
        ↓                        [does the regex match this line?]
SEAM 2  .github/renovate.json:59-61  matchStrings
        ↓                        [does depName name a real Debian package?]
SEAM 3  datasourceTemplate: "deb"   (renovate.json:62)
        ↓                        [do the registryUrls address suites that exist?]
SEAM 4  packageRules[].registryUrls (renovate.json:26-30, 36-40)
        ↓                        [does the archive answer? ← the no-result seam]
SEAM 5  deb.debian.org
        ↓                        [does a PR get opened?]
SEAM 6  Renovate PR → automerge (renovate.json:10)
        ↓                        [does the merged ARG value install?]
SEAM 7  android.Dockerfile:164   openjdk-17-jdk-headless="$OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION"
        ↓                        [do apt's sources match renovate's registryUrls?]
SEAM 8  config/debian_12_bookworm.sources ↔ renovate.json packageRules
        ↓
        docker build
```

**Verification status of each seam:**

| Seam | Verified by | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — annotation → regex | **NOTHING** | Silent (this is the #317 rename bug, 2026-06-08) |
| 2 — depName correctness | **NOTHING** | Silent-then-wrong (the `ruby-dev`/`ruby-full` bug, archived proposal:10) |
| 3 — datasource selection | `renovate-config-validator --strict` (schema only) | Silent |
| 4 — registryUrls → suites | **NOTHING** | Silent (this is issue #532, 10 weeks) |
| 5 — archive lookup | **NOTHING** | `no-result` at DEBUG. **The bug.** |
| 6 — PR opened | **NOTHING** (absence of PRs is invisible) | Silent |
| 7 — apt install | `ci.yml:74-90` / `build.yml` build-image | **LOUD — build fails** |
| 8 — sources ↔ registryUrls | **NOTHING** | Silent |

**Seven of eight seams have no verification. The one that does (seam 7) is the last one, and it fails by breaking the build on `main`.**

### B.2 The single component everything passes through

**`.github/renovate.json`.** Every one of the nine pins, both datasources (deb + github-tags for gx.toml), the automerge decision, the scheduling, and now the suite selection all funnel through this one 65-line file. Seams 2, 3, 4, and 6 are all *inside* it.

And it is the one file in the repo with **zero automated verification** (A.3). The concentration of unverified seams is not incidental — every seam that lacks verification lacks it *because* it lives in or crosses this file, and this file has no checker.

Compare the parallel structure for GitHub Actions: `.github/gx.toml` is *also* a single funnel for every action version — but it has `gx lint` (`gx.yml:36-39`) verifying manifest↔lock↔workflow agreement, and `gx tidy` (`gx.yml:73-76`) auto-repairing drift. The repo already knows how to guard a funnel. It did it for actions and not for apt pins.

### B.3 The seam nobody has named: seam 8

`config/debian_12_bookworm.sources:5,11` says `Suites: bookworm bookworm-updates` / `bookworm-security` with `Components: main contrib non-free non-free-firmware`. PR #531's `renovate.json:37-39` restates the same three suites and same four components as URLs. PR #531's own `design.md:66` acknowledges this: "Mirroring keeps the invariant checkable by eye."

**"Checkable by eye" is the state seam 4 was in for ten weeks.** Two files restating the same fact with no cross-check is exactly the "two vocabularies, two files, nothing cross-checks them" pattern Step 1 identified for `suite=` vs `release`. PR #531 removes one instance of that pattern and introduces another.

Note also: `android.Dockerfile:1` pins `debian:13.6-slim` by digest, so the trixie/trixie-updates/trixie-security half of the mirror (`renovate.json:26-30`) has **no in-repo counterpart at all** — it mirrors a sources file that exists only inside the base image. That half is not even eye-checkable.

---

## C. WHAT THE 17→21 MIGRATION ACTUALLY TOUCHES

### C.1 Is 21 in trixie?

**Could not verify — network egress to deb.debian.org is blocked in this environment** (`curl` to `https://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/trixie/Release` returns `000`, both sandboxed and with sandbox disabled). This is the same constraint PR #531 hit (`design.md:76`, `tasks.md:26`).

From package-tracker knowledge, **flagged as needing confirmation**: Debian 13 trixie ships `openjdk-21-jdk-headless` (21.x) as its default JDK, and also carries `openjdk-25-*` in some form. Trixie does **not** carry openjdk-17 — which is precisely why `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` exists (`android.Dockerfile:149`: "Add debian 12 bookworm repository alongside debian 13 trixie to install Java 17").

The one-line confirmation, runnable in any CI job with egress:
`curl -s https://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/trixie/main/binary-amd64/Packages.gz | zcat | grep -A1 '^Package: openjdk-21-jdk-headless'`

### C.2 Every file and line the migration touches

**Files that MUST change (4):**

| Location | Current | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `android.Dockerfile:143` | `# renovate: depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless` (PR #531 form) | → `openjdk-21-jdk-headless` |
| `android.Dockerfile:144` | `ARG OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1"` | → `ARG OPENJDK_21_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="<trixie version>"` — **name changes too**, so also line 164 |
| `android.Dockerfile:140` | `JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64` | → `java-21-openjdk-amd64`. **HAND-TYPED, nothing checks it** (Step 1). Guarded by `TODO`s at `:136-138` referencing moby/moby#29110 |
| `android.Dockerfile:164` | `openjdk-17-jdk-headless="$OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION" \` | → `openjdk-21-jdk-headless="$OPENJDK_21_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION" \` |
| `.github/renovate.json:33-40` (PR #531) | The entire `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` bookworm override packageRule | **DELETED** — 8 lines, all three bookworm registryUrls gone |

**Files DELETED (1):**

| Location | Notes |
|---|---|
| `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` (13 lines, whole file) | Exists solely for Java 17 (line 1: "to install Java 17") |
| `android.Dockerfile:150` | `COPY config/debian_12_bookworm.sources /etc/apt/sources.list.d/...` — deleted |
| `android.Dockerfile:168-169` | `# Delete debian 12 bookworm repository after installing Java 17` + `&& rm /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian_12_bookworm.sources \` — deleted |
| `android.Dockerfile:149` | The comment "Add debian 12 bookworm repository alongside debian 13 trixie to install Java 17" — deleted |

**Files that change AUTOMATICALLY (2) — do not hand-edit:**

| Location | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| `config/version.json:13-15` (`"java": {"version": 17}`) | Derived by `.github/workflows/update-version.yml:296-303` running `script/java_version.sh` **inside the previously-published image**. Will read 17 until an image with 21 ships — **a one-cycle lag by construction** |
| `test/android.yml:34-40` (`expectedOutput: ["17"]`) | Generated by `script/update_test.sh:16,26` from `config/version.json` via `config/android.cue:33,56-61`. `build.yml:392-414` (`validate-generated-config`) enforces it as a git fixed point |

**Files that DO NOT change (5) — verified by reading, not assumed:**

| Location | Why not |
|---|---|
| `config/schema.cue:46` | `java!: #PlatformVersion` = `{version!: int}` (`schema.cue:4-6`). Version-agnostic. |
| `config/android.cue:33,54-61` | Templated on the tag `android_java_version`, not a literal. |
| `readme.md` | **Grepped: contains no `java`, `Java`, `JDK`, `17`, or `Debian` anywhere.** Java is not displayed. |
| `docs/build.mjs` | Grepped for java/jdk/17/debian: zero hits. It maps only `v.flutter.version` (`build.mjs:19`) and pull badges. |
| `docs/contributing.md:15` | Lists "Flutter, Fastlane, Gradle, NDK, …" generically, no Java version literal. |

> **Correction to the task brief:** `readme.md` and `docs/build.mjs` are listed as things to check for the migration. They are **clean** — Java never reaches the rendered docs. `openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-20-readme-platform-tool-lists/design.md:11` says the README *should* show Java, and `:54` claims a README↔manifest↔image chain, but the current committed `readme.md` (73 lines, read in full) shows no Java at all. **The `config/version.json` `android.java` field and the `script/java_version.sh` derivation currently feed nothing user-visible — only the `test/android.yml` self-assertion.**

### C.3 The migration's net structural effect

**Deleting the openjdk-17 pin deletes the only reason Debian 12 exists in this repo.** After migration:
- `renovate.json` drops from 2 deb packageRules to 1, and the load-bearing rule-ordering constraint (`renovate.json:33`, "Must stay after the trixie rule") **disappears**
- All 9 pins resolve against the same 3 trixie URLs
- `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` is gone, so seam 8 (B.3) has nothing to mirror
- `android.Dockerfile` loses the COPY/rm pair — the two-suite apt window closes
- Every `deb1?u` literal (`android.Dockerfile:8,10,144,146`) becomes `deb13u`-only — the 3 substring-embedded release statements Step 1 counted collapse to one vocabulary

### C.4 Does anything constrain the JDK from the Flutter/AGP side?

Grepped `gradle|agp|kotlin|jdk|java` across all `.md`, `.cue`, `.json`, `.kts`, `.yml`. **No JDK version constraint exists anywhere in the repo.**

- `script/updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts` — derives `gradleVersion`, `ndk`, `buildTools` from AGP. Does **not** touch Java.
- `android.Dockerfile:217` — `RUN ./gradlew --version`, a smoke check only, no version assertion
- `test/android.yml:3-21` — `./gradlew bundleRelease` under the shipped JDK; this is the **only real AGP↔JDK compatibility test in the repo, and it is empirical** (it either builds or it doesn't)
- `openspec/changes/archive/2026-05-27-fix-android-buildtools-resolution/design.md:16-21` establishes AGP 9.0.1 / build-tools 36.0.0 as the current AGP generation. **AGP 9 requires JDK 17 as a floor and supports 21.** The 17→21 direction is upward-compatible; nothing in-repo forbids it.
- `config/version.json:16-18` — Gradle 9.1.0, which supports running on JDK 21.

**Conclusion: the constraint is empirical, not declared.** The only thing that would object to JDK 21 is `test/android.yml:3-21` failing at build time — the same place, and the same lateness, as every other failure in this system (Step 1's "no in-image assertion can catch this class").

---

## D. THE BOUNDARY THAT WOULD MAKE BOTH ITEMS CHEAPER OR UNNECESSARY

### D.1 The boundary as currently drawn

> **"Renovate config is Renovate's business. The repo's business is `config/version.json`."**

Everything the repo treats as a version-with-verification lives in `config/version.json` and gets: a CUE type (`config/schema.cue`), a `cue vet` CI job (`build.yml:372-390`), a generated-artifact fixed point (`build.yml:392-414`), a docs render (`docs/build.mjs`), and a derivation job (`update-version.yml`). Nine values, five mechanisms.

Everything on the other side of the boundary — the nine apt pins — lives in `android.Dockerfile` comments plus `.github/renovate.json`, and gets: **a script nobody calls.**

`config/version.json` has no Debian concept (`schema.cue:41-57`: flutter, android, fastlane, windows — that's the whole type). It cannot have one, because the boundary says apt versions are Renovate's business.

### D.2 Why that boundary is what makes both items expensive

**Item 2 (the CI guard) is expensive only because of where the boundary sits.** Asserting "every extracted deb pin yields a lookup result" requires a live Renovate dry-run against deb.debian.org — network egress, a `npx renovate` install, ~minutes of CI, and a check that goes red when Debian's mirror is slow. The reason it must ask the network is that **the repo holds no local statement of what the answer should be.** There is no committed fact that says "openjdk-17-jdk-headless is expected to resolve, from these three suites." The only place that intent is written is the `registryUrls` array itself — so the guard cannot compare the config against anything; it can only go ask the world.

Contrast `validate-generated-config` (`build.yml:392-414`): that job is hermetic and 10 seconds *because* `config/version.json` and `test/android.yml` are two committed representations of the same fact, and the check is "regenerate one from the other and diff." The repo already owns this pattern. It cannot apply it to deb pins because the deb pins' intent is single-sourced in a file with no schema.

**Item 3 (the 17→21 decision) is expensive only because "which Debian release" is undefined.** Step 1 counted it stated 21 times across 4 files and defined nowhere. C.2 above confirms the shape: to answer "can we drop bookworm?" a maintainer must read `android.Dockerfile:1` (the digest), `:143-144` (the pin), `:149-150,168-169` (the COPY/rm), `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` (13 lines), `renovate.json:26-40` (six URLs restating both), and the version literals at `:8,10,144,146` — and hold in their head that the `deb12u1` suffix on line 144 is *causally* why lines 149-150 and 168-169 exist. **The migration is not hard; discovering its extent is.** There is no single place that says "this image is built on Debian 13 trixie; one package is imported from Debian 12 bookworm; here is why."

### D.3 The boundary redrawn

**Bring "which Debian suites this image resolves against" inside `config/` as a declared, CUE-typed fact — the same status Flutter, Android, Fastlane, and Windows toolchain versions already have.**

Concretely, that one move does all of this:

- `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` stops being a hand-written apt file and becomes *generated* from the declaration — folding seam 8 into the existing `update_test.sh` / `git diff --exit-code` fixed-point pattern (`build.yml:412-414`). Seam 8's cross-check becomes free and hermetic.
- The `registryUrls` arrays in `renovate.json:26-40` become *generated* from the same declaration — closing seam 4 the same way. The "two vocabularies, nothing cross-checks them" pattern Step 1 found, and which PR #531 reintroduces in a new form (B.3), stops being possible by construction.
- **Item 3 collapses to editing one declaration.** "Which packages come from a non-default suite" becomes a single readable list with one entry (`openjdk-17-jdk-headless ← bookworm`). Deleting that entry *is* the migration; the COPY/rm and the packageRule and the sources file all regenerate to nothing. The question "what does 17→21 touch?" — which took C.2 to answer — becomes a one-line diff.
- **Item 2 shrinks from a network dry-run to a hermetic diff, for the failure modes that actually occurred.** Both real bugs (the #317 rename, seam 1; and #532's suite mismatch, seam 4) are *config-vs-config* disagreements, catchable by regeneration + diff with zero egress. Only seam 5 — "does the archive actually have this version?" — genuinely needs the network, and seam 5 is the one seam that is *already* covered loudly by the docker build (seam 7). The expensive network guard would be buying a second detector for the one seam that isn't silent.

### D.4 The sharpest statement of the finding

The repo has exactly one verification idiom, used three times, and it works: **commit two representations of a fact and diff them in CI** (`build.yml:392-414`, `update-docs.yml:49-57`, `gx.yml:78-93`). Every fact inside the `config/version.json` boundary gets it. Every fact outside gets nothing.

The nine apt pins are outside. So is "which Debian release." That is not because they're unsuitable — apt suites and their registryUrls are *the* textbook case of one fact needing two representations — it's because the boundary was drawn around `config/version.json` before there was a second Debian suite to reason about.

Both remaining items land where they do (an orphan network-dependent workflow; a hand-traced multi-file archaeology) **only because that boundary leaves nowhere better.** Moving it makes item 3 a one-line edit and reduces item 2 to the repo's existing 10-second hermetic pattern for the failures that have actually happened — leaving the genuine network question (seam 5) to the place that already answers it loudly.
Both findings are strong. Now step 3 — the topic itself. Let me verify the key factual claims: is openjdk-21 in trixie, and what are the Renovate/AGP constraints.

#-----------------------------------------------

FROM fastlane AS android

SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-euxo", "pipefail", "-c"]

# TODO: Get JAVA_HOME dinamically from a JDK binary
# TODO: Use `dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(which javac)))` after the following issue is fixed
# TODO: https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/29110
ENV ANDROID_HOME="$SDK_ROOT/android-sdk" \
    JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
ENV PATH="$PATH:$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$HOME/.local/bin"

# renovate: suite=bookworm depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless
ARG OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1"
# renovate: suite=trixie depName=sudo
ARG SUDO_VERSION="1.9.16p2-3+deb13u2"

USER root
# Add debian 12 bookworm repository alongside debian 13 trixie to install Java 17
COPY config/debian_12_bookworm.sources /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian_12_bookworm.sources
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    # For Android x86 emulators
    # libxtst6=2:1.2.3-1build4 \
    # libnss3-dev=2:3.68.2-0ubuntu1.1 \
    # libnspr4=2:4.32-3build1 \
    # libxss1=1:1.2.3-1build2 \
    # libasound2=1.2.6.1-1ubuntu1 \
    # libatk-bridge2.0-0=2.38.0-3 \
    # libgtk-3-0=3.24.33-1ubuntu2 \
    # libgdk-pixbuf2.0-0=2.40.2-2build4 \
    # Android SDK dependencies
    ## JDK needs to be used instead of JRE because it provides the jlink tool used by the Android build
    openjdk-17-jdk-headless="$OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION" \
    # To allow changing ownership in GitLab CI /builds
    sudo="$SUDO_VERSION" \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    # Delete debian 12 bookworm repository after installing Java 17
    && rm /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian_12_bookworm.sources \
    # To allow changing ownership in GitLab CI /builds
    && echo "flutter ALL= NOPASSWD:/bin/chown -R flutter /builds, /bin/chown -R flutter /builds/*" >> /etc/sudoers.d/flutter

USER flutter:flutter
WORKDIR "$HOME"

ARG android_build_tools_version
ARG android_platform_versions
ARG android_ndk_version
ARG cmake_version

Here's what the search turned up on Flutter, AGP, and JDK 21 compatibility:

## The core issue

The most common failure mode is a version mismatch across the toolchain. This error typically occurs due to a mismatch between the versions of the Java Development Kit (JDK), Android SDK, Gradle, and Flutter. The classic symptom is a `JdkImageTransform` failure: "Failed to transform core-for-system-modules.jar" followed by an error executing `jlink`.

The root cause: jlink creates a custom Java runtime environment tailored for your app, but older versions of the Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) — specifically those before version 8.2.1 — contain a bug that breaks when jlink and JDK 21 are used together.

## Version requirements

- **AGP ≥ 8.2.1** is the practical floor for JDK 21 support.
- **Gradle ≥ 8.5** is required for JDK 21. Android Studio Ladybug (2024.2.1) ships with JDK 21, which is incompatible with Gradle below 8.5, causing build failures.
- Older Gradle has narrower ranges — for example, Gradle 8.3 requires Java 17 ≤ version < Java 21.
- If you're targeting compileSdk 35: "Using compileSdk 35 requires Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 8.1.0 or higher."

## Fixes

Based on the page content, here's what's actually documented — and importantly, what **isn't**:

## What the page explicitly states

**No support table exists on this page.** This is a narrow breaking-change migration guide, not a compatibility reference. It contains no matrix of JDK ↔ Gradle ↔ AGP versions, no stated minimum JDK, and no stated maximum JDK.

### Explicit version numbers mentioned

| Item | Value stated |
|---|---|
| Gradle versions that work with Java 17 | **7.3 through 7.6.1, inclusive** (repeated as the recommended range) |
| Gradle versions that **cannot** run under Java 17 | Anything **prior to 7.3** (links to [Gradle's compatibility matrix](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/compatibility.html#java)) |
| Android Studio Flamingo bundled JDK | Upgraded from **11 → 17** |
| Example JDK path given | `openjdk@17` (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/openjdk@17/17.0.13/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home`) |
| Class file major version 61 | = Java 17 (error under old Gradle) |
| Class file major version 65 | = Java 21 (mentioned only as an error symptom) |

### Is JDK 21 supported?

The page **never says**. JDK 21 appears only implicitly, as a failure mode:

> The error appears similar to `Unsupported class file major version 65`. This is an indication that your Java version is newer than the version of Gradle you are running can handle. There is a non-obvious set of dependencies surrounding AGP, Java, and Gradle.

Major version 65 corresponds to Java 21, but the doc doesn't name it, doesn't say which Gradle/AGP versions pair with it, and gives no minimum/maximum. It explicitly punts to tooling rather than publishing numbers.

## The compatibility relationship

The page acknowledges a three-way dependency but deliberately declines to enumerate it — "a non-obvious set of dependencies surrounding AGP, Java, and Gradle." Instead it directs you to two resolution paths:

**Android Studio:** Select your top-level `build.gradle`, then **Tools → AGP Upgrade Assistant**.

**Command line:**

```sh
flutter analyze --suggestions      # reports whether AGP/Java/Gradle are compatible
flutter doctor                     # reports the Java version in use
flutter doctor -v                  # reports which Java version Flutter resolved
```

Then apply the version `flutter analyze` suggests:

```sh
cd android
./gradlew wrapper REDACTED
```

Note the doc says "you can use a newer version" than suggested — so the 7.3–7.6.1 ceiling is specific to the Flamingo/JDK 17 scenario, not a global cap.

### Java resolution order (explicit)

1. The JDK bundled with Android Studio (Flutter's default)
2. `JAVA_HOME` if Android Studio isn't installed
3. Any `java` on `PATH`

Override globally:

```sh
flutter config --jdk-dir=SOMEJAVAPATH
```

On macOS, enumerate installed JDKs with `/usr/libexec/java_home -V`.

## Caveats worth flagging

The page carries an explicit staleness warning:

> These breaking change docs are accurate, as of the release under which they are published. Over time, the workarounds described here might become inaccurate. We don't, in general, keep these breaking change docs up to date as of each release.

It also warns that Gradle **newer than 7.6.1** may introduce issues from deprecated Gradle classes or Android file-structure changes, with the remedy being to downgrade back into 7.3–7.6.1. And: "Upgrading to Flutter 3.10 won't fix this issue."

**Bottom line:** if you need an authoritative JDK/Gradle/AGP matrix — particularly for JDK 21 — this page won't give it to you. Run `flutter analyze --suggestions` against your actual project, or consult Gradle's own [Java compatibility matrix](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/compatibility.html#java), which this page links to precisely because it doesn't reproduce those numbers itself.

## Renovate `deb` Datasource — Documentation Summary

### Table of values
| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| Identifier | `deb` |
| Default versioning | `deb` |
| Custom registry support | Yes |
| Release timestamp support | No |
| Source URL support | No |

### Description
This datasource handles package updates sourced from Debian repositories, aimed at projects relying on Debian-based systems or derivative distributions such as Ubuntu. Detection is not automatic — the docs state that "By default, Renovate does not detect Debian dependencies," and that pairing the datasource with regex/custom managers is required.

### registryUrl format and query parameters
A correctly structured URL with query parameters must be supplied as the `registryUrl`. The page documents three parameters (note: **no `release` parameter is described** in this document):

- `components` — "Comma-separated list of repository components (e.g., `main,contrib,non-free`)."
- `binaryArch` — "Architecture of the binary packages (e.g., `amd64`,`all`)."
- `suite` — either "A rolling release alias like `stable`." or "A fixed release name such as `bullseye` or `buster`."

An important caveat appears in a note: "These parameters are used to give Renovate context and are not directly used to call the repository." Consequently, the docs add that the `registryUrl` "has not to be a valid URL for a repository."

Sample URL given: `https://deb.debian.org/debian?suite=stable&components=main,contrib,non-free&binaryArch=amd64`, which the page explains targets the stable suite for amd64 across the main, contrib, and non-free components.

### registryStrategy and multiple registryUrls
**Not covered.** The provided page does not mention a `registryStrategy` value, nor does it explain how several `registryUrls` entries would be merged, prioritized, or iterated. The only multi-URL-adjacent content is an example showing how a `packageRules` entry with `matchDatasources: ["deb"]` and `matchPackageNames` can override the registry URL for a specific package (e.g., `gcc-11`).

### Packages that fail to resolve
**Not covered.** The document contains no notes about unresolvable packages, error handling, or fallback behavior.

### Usage example (Dockerfile pinning)
A custom regex manager targeting `Dockerfile` extracts `suite`, `depName`, and `currentValue` from a preceding comment, with a `registryUrlTemplate` that defaults the suite to `stable` when none is captured, and `datasourceTemplate` set to `deb`. Dockerfile comments like `# renovate: suite=bullseye depName=gcc-11` sit above an `ENV GCC_VERSION="11.2.0-19"` line; the environment variable is then bumped when a new apt package version appears.

### Artifactory support
Supported repository types are virtual, local, and remote. The registryUrl pattern shown is `https://<host>:<port>/artifactory/<repository-slug>?suite=<suite>&components=<components>&binaryArch=<binaryArch>`, e.g. an Artifactory host with `suite=bookworm`. For protected instances, generate a password via Artifactory's "Set Me Up" feature and configure a `hostRules` entry using `hostType: "deb"`, a `matchHost` covering the repository path, plus `username` and `password`.

Here's what the search results show about how Renovate surfaces `no-result` lookup failures:

## How the warning surfaces

Renovate reports lookup failures in two places on the Dependency Dashboard issue:

1. **A "Repository problems" section** near the top. Under "Renovate tried to run on this repository, but found these problems," it lists "WARN: Package lookup failures."

2. **An inline warning block** listing the unresolvable dependencies plus the files they came from. The warning reads "Renovate failed to look up the following dependencies:" followed by each failed package, then a "Files affected:" line naming the specific manifest paths.

## The `no-result` variant

The bare form (`Failed to look up docker package X`) appears without a reason, but the `no-result` suffix shows up when the datasource returned an empty response:

- "Failed to look up terraform-provider package schwitzd/garage: no-result" with files affected spanning `terraform/garage/main.tf` and a nested module file
- Custom datasources hit it too: "Failed to look up custom.grafana-dashboards package 25155: no-result, Failed to look up custom.grafana-dashboards package 25156: no-result," affecting a single `grafanadashboard.yaml`

## Distinct failure modes are grouped together

Notably, `no-result` is only one of several lookup error strings Renovate concatenates into the same warning. One large repo's dashboard mixes them: "Could not determine new digest for update (docker package ghcr.io/fredrikburmester/streamystats-nextjs)" appears alongside "Failed to look up docker package quay.io/csiaddons/k8s-controller: no-result" and "Failed to look up docker package quay.io/backube/volsync: no-result" — so digest-resolution failures and empty-registry-response failures share one surface.

## Common triggers visible in the results

The affected packages cluster around a few patterns:

- **Private/self-hosted registries** — a GitLab-hosted image referenced from its own repo's `docker-compose.yml` files fails lookup, and three `registry.gitlab.com` .NET runtime-deps images fail simultaneously. Typically an auth/`hostRules` gap.
- **Regex/custom managers producing non-real package names** — a `regex` manager extracts `debian_13/clamav` and `google/go-containerregistry` as docker deps, both of which fail lookup. These aren't Docker Hub paths, so the datasource is mismatched.
- **Genuinely bogus names** — test fixtures like `baseasAsSa`, `test-image1`, and `test1_l-3` in a Dockerfile all surface as lookup failures, confirming the warning fires on typos too.
- **Non-default datasources** — a `gitlab-tags` package (`hoverkraft-tech/ci-gitlab-common`, referenced in `.gitlab-ci.yml`) failing lookup.

## Practical read

`no-result` means the datasource was reached but returned no versions — as opposed to a network/auth error, which usually produces a different message. The results suggest checking, in order: whether the datasource is correct for the extracted name (the regex-manager cases), whether credentials are configured for private registries (the `registry.gitlab.com` cases), and whether the package name is simply wrong (the fixture cases).

One caveat: the dashboard still reports "These updates have all been created already" alongside the warning, so a `no-result` failure doesn't block the rest of the run — it silently drops just those deps from update consideration, which is why it's easy to miss without watching the dashboard.

input.prompt: Does the Dependency Dashboard list dependencies detected by custom/regex managers in its "Detected Dependencies" section? What determines whether a manager's dependencies appear there? Also: what is dependencyDashboardReportAbandonment and how are package lookup failures / warnings surfaced on the dashboard — quote any text about "Repository problems" or lookup warnings.

content.content:
The provided page content doesn't answer most of what you're asking. Here's what is and isn't covered:

**Not covered in the supplied text:**
- Whether custom/regex managers' dependencies show in the Dependency Dashboard's "Detected Dependencies" section
- What determines a manager's inclusion in that section
- "Repository problems" text or how lookup failures/warnings are surfaced

The page is a table of contents plus the option entries from `abandonmentThreshold` through roughly `constraintsFiltering` — the content was truncated before reaching the `dependencyDashboard*` option bodies. The dashboard options are only listed as anchor links (e.g. `dependencyDashboard`, `dependencyDashboardHeader`, `dependencyDashboardOSVVulnerabilitySummary`), with no descriptive text.

**Partially covered — `dependencyDashboardReportAbandonment`:**

Only the anchor link appears; its description is not in the excerpt. However, the related `abandonmentThreshold` option is documented and gives useful context. It "Flags packages that have not been updated within this period as abandoned," and Renovate attaches an `isAbandoned` boolean to lookup results when the threshold is defined and the package has a `mostRecentTimestamp` from the datasource. That timestamp "represents the release date of the highest version," but counts only if that version is also the newest by time. A package gets marked abandoned if its latest release date plus the threshold duration has already passed. Values are duration strings such as `2 years` or `90 days`, and it can be scoped via `packageRules`. Given the naming, `dependencyDashboardReportAbandonment` almost certainly controls surfacing those flags on the dashboard — but I can't confirm that from this text.

**One tangentially relevant item that is documented — `configWarningReuseIssue`:**

This concerns config warnings rather than lookup warnings. Renovate by default opens a fresh issue per warning, "although never more than one open at a time." Set it to `true` and Renovate will "reopen any found matching closed issue whenever there is a config warning," with the tradeoff that an old issue keeps getting "recycled" and sorts older than others.

To get real answers on detected dependencies and repository problems, check the Key concepts → Dependency Dashboard page or the untruncated `dependencyDashboard*` sections of this same document.

The page provided doesn't cover most of what you're asking about, so I can only answer partially.

**Not covered in this page:**
- There is no mention of a "Repository problems" section, package lookup failures, or a "Detected Dependencies" section — so I can't quote text about those or say whether custom/regex manager dependencies appear there.
- There is no statement about how often the dashboard issue gets refreshed or whether it's rewritten on every Renovate run.

**What the page does say about surfacing problems:**

Deprecation warnings are the one problem-surfacing behavior described. When Renovate encounters "packages flagged as deprecated on their registry, or" packages having "a community-sourced replacement PR available," it "adds a prominent warning about these packages near the top of the Dependency Dashboard." The sample table shown lists the datasource, package name, and whether a replacement exists (e.g. `airbnb-prop-types` marked available, `left-pad` unavailable).

Related to this, abandonment detection is offered via a preset that "Sets a default `abandonmentThreshold` of `1 year` for all packages" and "Prevents updates to truly abandoned packages while allowing updates to packages with irregular release schedules."

The dashboard also gives "Visibility into rejected/deferred updates" — an overview of "all updates that are still 'to do'." Declining a PR without merging puts that update in the Closed/Ignored area, and you can recover it later: "you can get a new PR by selecting the corresponding checkbox on the dashboard."

If you need the answers on repository problems, detected dependencies, and update cadence, you'd want the Renovate configuration options reference or the dashboard source, not this key-concepts page.

Yes — there is a strict equality dependency. The three Depends entries listed on that page are:

- **libc6** — `(>= 2.34)`
- **openjdk-21-jre-headless** — `(= 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2)`
- **zlib1g** — `(>= 1:1.1.4)`

The relevant line reads exactly: "dep: openjdk-21-jre-headless (= 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2)"

So the headless JDK is pinned to the identical binary version of its runtime counterpart, matching the package's own version (21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2). The other two dependencies use minimum-version constraints instead, and both are described briefly on the page — libc6 as the "GNU C Library: Shared libraries" and zlib1g as a "compression library - runtime".

input.content:
# Research: making apt-pin resolution failure loud (issue #532, items 2 & 3)

Scope: issue #532 item 1 is done (PR #531). This researches the two open items:

- **Item 2** — make silent Renovate resolution failure loud.
- **Item 3** — decide whether to migrate openjdk-17 → openjdk-21.

## Headline

**Item 2 is already built — by Renovate, at WARN level, on the Dependency
Dashboard. It did not fire because this repo's dashboard (issue #8) has been
stale since 2026-07-12 while Renovate kept running.** The issue's premise that
`no-result` is "logged at debug level only" is incorrect. Building a
network-dry-run CI guard would be reimplementing a mechanism the repo already
pays for and is not reading.

**Item 3's stated main benefit does not survive checking.** `openjdk-21-jdk-headless`
carries the *same* strict-equality sibling constraint as 17. The migration is
still worth doing, but for suite-consolidation and CVE reasons — not because it
removes the strict-sibling hazard.

---

## Context

What exists today, after PR #531 lands.

```
  android.Dockerfile                    .github/renovate.json
  ┌──────────────────────────┐          ┌─────────────────────────────┐
  │ # renovate: depName=curl │─────────▶│ customManagers[1]           │
  │ ARG CURL_VERSION="…"     │  regex   │   matchStrings              │
  │        × 9 pins          │          │   datasourceTemplate: deb   │
  └──────────────────────────┘          │                             │
                                        │ packageRules                │
  config/debian_12_bookworm.sources     │  ├─ deb → trixie ×3   (main)│
  ┌──────────────────────────┐          │  └─ openjdk-17 → bookworm ×3│
  │ Suites: bookworm …       │◀ ─ ─ ─ ─▶│       (4 components)        │
  │ Components: main contrib…│  "checkable  └─────────────────────────┘
  └──────────────────────────┘   by eye"              │
                                                      ▼
                                              deb.debian.org
```

Nine pins, all in `android.Dockerfile`: `curl:8`, `git:10`, `lcov:12`,
`ca-certificates:14`, `unzip:16`, `ruby-full:97`, `build-essential:99`,
`openjdk-17-jdk-headless:144`, `sudo:146`. Eight resolve against trixie; one
against bookworm, added solely because trixie has no openjdk-17
(`android.Dockerfile:149`).

The verification surface (11 workflows). `build.yml:372-444` holds three
hermetic, ~10s, no-`needs:` config jobs — `validate-version-files` (`cue vet`),
`validate-generated-config` (`update_test.sh` + `git diff --exit-code`),
`build-docs`. This is the repo's meta lane and its one verification idiom:
**commit two representations of a fact and diff them in CI** (used at
`build.yml:412-414`, `update-docs.yml:49-57`, `gx.yml:78-93`).

`script/renovate_validate.sh` runs `renovate-config-validator --strict`. It is
invoked by **nothing** — grep across all workflows, `mise.toml` and scripts
returns zero call sites. Its only references are `- [x]` checkboxes in change
documents (`openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/tasks.md:4`,
and PR #531's `tasks.md:23`). `.github/renovate.json` is the only significant
config file in the repo with no automated verification.

---

## Findings

### F1 — Renovate already surfaces this at WARN, on the dashboard

Traced through Renovate's source:

1. Lookup fails → `res.warnings.push({topic, message: 'Failed to look up deb package X: no-result'})`
   — `lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/index.ts:291-303`. The `logger.debug`
   at :295 that the issue cites is *adjacent to*, not instead of, the warnings push.
2. `getDepWarnings()` collects every `dep.warnings` and calls
   **`logger.warn({warnings, files}, 'Package lookup failures')`** —
   `lib/workers/repository/errors-warnings.ts:59-61`. **WARN, not debug.**
3. `getDepWarningsDashboard()` renders "⚠️ **Warning** Renovate failed to look up
   the following dependencies: … Files affected: …" — `errors-warnings.ts:112-138`.
4. It is written into the dashboard issue body at
   `lib/workers/repository/dependency-dashboard.ts:563-567`.

The only gate is `config.suppressNotifications?.includes('dependencyLookupWarnings')`
(`errors-warnings.ts:116`). **`.github/renovate.json` sets no `suppressNotifications`.**
Third-party dashboards confirm the rendered form in the wild, `no-result` included
— e.g. [trueforge-org/truecharts#18710](https://github.com/trueforge-org/truecharts/issues/18710).

So the correct-by-construction alarm existed the whole time and was not muted.

### F2 — The real defect: the Dependency Dashboard is stale, and nobody noticed

Issue #8 (`Dependency Dashboard`, author `app/renovate`):

| Signal | Value |
|---|---|
| `updatedAt` (body last written) | **2026-07-12T18:49:17Z** |
| Renovate still running? | **Yes** — PR #528 opened 2026-08-06 |
| Timeline `referenced` events | …2026-07-15, 2026-07-18, **2026-08-06** |

The body proves the staleness independently of the timestamp. It lists
`.github/workflows/update_version.yml`, `tag.yml` and `changelog.yml` — all three
**gone** from the repo (current names are hyphenated: `update-version.yml`, and
`tag.yml`/`changelog.yml` no longer exist). It shows `debian 13.2-slim` while
`android.Dockerfile:1` is at 13.6.

It also contains **no Detected Dependencies entry for any of the nine deb pins** —
zero occurrences of `curl`, `sudo`, `ruby`, `lcov`, `unzip`, `build-essential`,
`ca-certificates`, `openjdk`, or `custom` in a 12,183-char body — and no
"Repository problems" / "Failed to look up" section.

```
   Renovate runs                Dashboard issue #8
   ─────────────                ──────────────────
   2026-07-12  ──────────────▶  body written ✓  ← last good render
   2026-07-15  ─────╮
   2026-07-18  ─────┤
   2026-08-06  ─────╯ ✗ referenced, body never rewritten
                        ▲
                        └─ the openjdk no-result warning would
                           have rendered HERE, every run, for 10 weeks
```

This is a **second, unreported bug**, and it is the one that actually caused the
ten weeks of silence. Root-causing it is cheaper and higher-value than building a
new guard. Two candidate mechanisms, both checkable from the next job log:
Renovate erroring before the dashboard write, or the config-migration checkbox at
the top of the body (`<!-- create-config-migration-pr -->`, currently `[x]`)
leaving the repo in a state where the body is not refreshed. Not resolvable from
outside the Mend job log — see Open Questions.

### F3 — Eight of nine seams have no verification; the ninth fails by breaking main

```
 SEAM 1  annotation ─────────▶ regex match          ✗ nothing   (#317-class bug)
 SEAM 2  depName ────────────▶ real package?        ✗ nothing   (ruby-dev/full bug)
 SEAM 3  datasource ─────────▶ deb                  ~ schema only
 SEAM 4  registryUrls ───────▶ suites exist?        ✗ nothing   ← #532
 SEAM 5  archive lookup ─────▶ versions             ✗ in-repo   ← F1 covers this
 SEAM 6  PR opened ──────────▶ (absence invisible)  ✗ nothing
 SEAM 7  apt install ────────▶ docker build         ✓✓ LOUD — breaks main
 SEAM 8  .sources ↔ registryUrls                    ✗ nothing
```

Everything funnels through `.github/renovate.json` — seams 2, 3, 4 and 6 are all
*inside* it, and it is the one config file with no checker. Contrast `.github/gx.toml`,
an equivalent funnel, which has `gx lint` + `gx tidy` (`gx.yml:36-39,73-76`).

Note what a network dry-run guard would actually buy: it detects **seam 5**, the
one seam already covered loudly (by F1's dashboard warning, and by seam 7's build
failure). Seams 1, 2, 4 and 8 — where both real bugs happened — are
**config-vs-config** disagreements, catchable hermetically.

### F4 — Seam 8 is new, introduced by PR #531

`config/debian_12_bookworm.sources:5,11` and `renovate.json:37-39` now restate
the same three suites and four components. PR #531's own `design.md:66` calls this
"checkable by eye" — which is precisely the state seam 4 was in for ten weeks.
The trixie half (`renovate.json:26-30`) mirrors a sources file that exists only
*inside* `debian:13.6-slim`, so it is not even eye-checkable.

### F5 — gx is the wrong home

`gx 0.7.2` is a "CLI to manage Github Actions dependencies". `gx lint` has exactly
ten rules, all about `uses:` refs and workflow YAML security. Its inputs are
`.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**`, `gx.toml`, `gx.lock`; its egress is
api.github.com. It has no concept of Dockerfiles, apt, deb, or datasources. The
boundary is already reasoned in
`openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/proposal.md:19`.
The memory "workflow lint belongs in gx" holds — this is not workflow lint.

### F6 — Item 3: openjdk-21 has the *same* strict-sibling constraint

Verified on [packages.debian.org/trixie/openjdk-21-jdk-headless](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/openjdk-21-jdk-headless):

- Version **`21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2`**, component **main**, trixie (stable).
- `Depends: openjdk-21-jre-headless (= 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2)`, `libc6 (>= 2.34)`, `zlib1g (>= 1:1.1.4)`.

**The strict `(=)` sibling is identical in shape to 17's.** The migration does
*not* remove the strict-sibling hazard. What it removes is the *governance gap*:
today the pin's sibling lives in a suite maintained by a different mechanism than
the pin. After migration, pin and sibling sit in the same suite set, so they
advance together — the same structural reason `curl`→`libcurl4t64 (= …)`
(`android.Dockerfile:8`) has never broken.

Migration surface, verified by reading:

**Changes (5 sites, all in 2 files):** `android.Dockerfile:143` (depName), `:144`
(ARG name *and* value — the major version is welded into the identifier
`OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION`), `:140` (`JAVA_HOME=…/java-17-openjdk-amd64`,
**hand-typed, guarded by nothing**, TODOs at `:136-138` blocked on
[moby/moby#29110](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/29110)), `:164` (install
line), and `renovate.json:33-40` (the whole bookworm packageRule, deleted — which
also deletes the load-bearing rule-ordering constraint).

**Deletions:** `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` (whole file),
`android.Dockerfile:149,150,168-169` (comment, COPY, rm).

**Regenerates automatically — do not hand-edit:** `config/version.json:13-15`
(derived by `update-version.yml:296-303` running `script/java_version.sh`
*inside the previously-published image*, so it lags one cycle by construction)
and `test/android.yml:34-40` (generated via `config/android.cue:33,56-61`,
enforced by `build.yml:392-414`).

**Unaffected (checked, not assumed):** `config/schema.cue:46` (`java!: #PlatformVersion`,
version-agnostic), `config/android.cue` (templated on a tag), `readme.md` (grepped:
contains no `java`/`JDK`/`17`/`Debian` at all), `docs/build.mjs` (zero hits).
Note: `config/version.json.android.java` currently feeds **nothing user-visible** —
only the `test/android.yml` self-assertion.

**AGP/Flutter constraint:** none declared anywhere in the repo. Grepped
`gradle|agp|kotlin|jdk|java` across all `.md`/`.cue`/`.json`/`.kts`/`.yml`. The
only real compatibility test is empirical — `test/android.yml:3-21` runs
`./gradlew bundleRelease` under the shipped JDK. Flutter's

```
lookup/index.ts:291-303   res.warnings.push({message: 'Failed to look up deb package X: no-result'})
errors-warnings.ts:59-61  logger.warn({warnings, files}, 'Package lookup failures')   ← WARN
errors-warnings.ts:112    getDepWarningsDashboard() renders "⚠️ Renovate failed to look up…"
dependency-dashboard.ts:563-567   written into the dashboard issue body
```

The only gate is `suppressNotifications: ['dependencyLookupWarnings']` (`errors-warnings.ts:116`) — **`.github/renovate.json` sets none.** The alarm existed, unmuted, the whole time.

### Finding 2 — the real bug: the Dependency Dashboard is stale

Issue #8 body last written **2026-07-12**; Renovate ran **2026-08-06** (PR #528). Proof independent of the timestamp: the body lists `update_version.yml`, `tag.yml`, `changelog.yml` — all three gone from the repo — and `debian 13.2-slim` while main is at 13.6. It contains zero mentions of any of the nine deb pins and no warnings section.

```
2026-07-12 ─▶ body written ✓   ← last good render
2026-07-15 ─╮
2026-07-18 ─┤ ✗ referenced, body never rewritten
2026-08-06 ─╯   ▲ the openjdk warning would have rendered here, every run
```

That is a second, unreported bug, and it's what actually caused the ten weeks of silence.

### Finding 3 — openjdk-21 has the *same* strict-sibling constraint

Verified on packages.debian.org: `openjdk-21-jdk-headless 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2` (trixie/main) has `Depends: openjdk-21-jre-headless (= 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2)`. The migration does **not** remove the strict-sibling hazard — it removes the *governance gap* (pin and sibling maintained by different mechanisms).

### Recommendations

**Item 2 — fix the dashboard, don't build the guard.** The proposed network dry-run detects seam 5 (does the archive answer?), the one seam already loud twice over — via the dashboard warning and via the build failing. Both bugs that actually happened (#317's rename, #532's suite mismatch) were *config-vs-config* disagreements, catchable hermetically in `build.yml`'s existing meta lane using the repo's own generate-and-`git diff --exit-code` idiom. Also: `script/renovate_validate.sh` is invoked by **nothing** — its only call sites are `- [x]` checkboxes in change docs.

**Item 3 — migrate, on corrected grounds.** Not for the sibling hazard, but because it deletes the bookworm sources file, the COPY/rm, the packageRule, the rule-ordering constraint, and the two-suite split. AGP 9.0.1 + Gradle 9.1.0 are well above the JDK 21 floors (AGP ≥ 8.2.1, Gradle ≥ 8.5). Fix the hand-typed unguarded `JAVA_HOME` (`android.Dockerfile:140`) in the same change. **Do item 3 first** — it makes item 2 nearly trivial.

Two side notes: the `{{#if release}}` typo was inherited from [Renovate's own deb docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/deb/), which document no `release` parameter yet ship that example (worth an upstream PR); and PR #531 introduces a new "checkable by eye" duplication between `debian_12_bookworm.sources` and its `registryUrls`.

Two open questions are in the report — the dashboard's failure mechanism needs the Mend job log, and whether the offered JDK is part of the image's contract is your call.

Sources: [Renovate deb datasource](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/deb/) · [openjdk-21-jdk-headless in trixie](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/openjdk-21-jdk-headless) · [Flutter Android Java Gradle migration guide](https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/android-java-gradle-migration-guide) · [example dashboard showing `no-result`](https://github.com/trueforge-org/truecharts/issues/18710)

### F2 — The real defect: the Dependency Dashboard is stale, and nobody noticed

Issue #8 (`Dependency Dashboard`, author `app/renovate`):

| Signal | Value |
|---|---|
| `updatedAt` (body last written) | **2026-07-12T18:49:17Z** |
| Renovate still running? | **Yes** — PR #528 opened 2026-08-06 |
| Timeline `referenced` events | …2026-07-15, 2026-07-18, **2026-08-06** |

The body proves the staleness independently of the timestamp. It lists
`.github/workflows/update_version.yml`, `tag.yml` and `changelog.yml` — all three
**gone** from the repo (current names are hyphenated: `update-version.yml`, and
`tag.yml`/`changelog.yml` no longer exist). It shows `debian 13.2-slim` while
`android.Dockerfile:1` is at 13.6.

It also contains **no Detected Dependencies entry for any of the nine deb pins** —
zero occurrences of `curl`, `sudo`, `ruby`, `lcov`, `unzip`, `build-essential`,
`ca-certificates`, `openjdk`, or `custom` in a 12,183-char body — and no
"Repository problems" / "Failed to look up" section.

```
   Renovate runs                Dashboard issue #8
   ─────────────                ──────────────────
   2026-07-12  ──────────────▶  body written ✓  ← last good render
   2026-07-15  ─────╮
   2026-07-18  ─────┤
   2026-08-06  ─────╯ ✗ referenced, body never rewritten
                        ▲
                        └─ the openjdk no-result warning would
                           have rendered HERE, every run, for 10 weeks
```

This is a **second, unreported bug**, and it is the one that actually caused the
ten weeks of silence. Root-causing it is cheaper and higher-value than building a
new guard. Two candidate mechanisms, both checkable from the next job log:
Renovate erroring before the dashboard write, or the config-migration checkbox at
the top of the body (`<!-- create-config-migration-pr -->`, currently `[x]`)
leaving the repo in a state where the body is not refreshed. Not resolvable from
outside the Mend job log — see Open Questions.
input.new_string:
### F2 — Root cause: the repository is running with `mode=silent`

**Confirmed from the Mend job log** (`gmeligio_flutter-docker-image_2026-08-07_14-50_019fdc2a…log`,
Renovate 44.12.0, 173 lines). The log contains, verbatim:

```
level 30  Repository is running with mode=silent and will not make Issues or PRs by default
level 20  Silent mode enabled so repo is considered onboarded
level 20  Dependency Dashboard issue is not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
level 20  Config migration issues are not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
level 20  Branch renovate/debian-13.6-slim creation is disabled because mode=silent
level 20  Branch renovate/mcr.microsoft.com-windows-servercore-ltsc2025 creation is disabled because mode=silent
```

The lookup failure **did** occur in this run —
`Failed to look up deb package openjdk-17-jdk-headless: no-result` — and per F1 it
was pushed onto `dep.warnings`, destined for the dashboard. Silent mode discarded
the delivery.

```
  F1: the alarm fires ────────────────────────────┐
                                                  │
  lookup fails → dep.warnings → getDepWarnings()  │  logger.warn ✓
                       │                          │
                       ▼                          │
             getDepWarningsDashboard()            │
                       │                          │
                       ▼                          │
             dependency-dashboard.ts:563 ─────────┤
                       │                          │
                       ▼                          │
             ✗ mode=silent — issue not written ◀──┘  THE SILENCE
```

Corroborating detail: the log's own level histogram is **168 debug / 6 info /
zero WARN**. The `logger.warn('Package lookup failures')` at
`errors-warnings.ts:59-61` does not appear — consistent with the log being
captured at a level that elides it, or with silent mode short-circuiting before
the aggregation. Either way the operator-facing signal is absent from the log too,
so *neither* channel (dashboard nor log warning) carried it.

`mode` is set **outside the repository**. It is absent from `.github/renovate.json`,
absent from the log's `File config`, `CLI config` and `Env config` objects — so it
comes from Mend's per-repository settings at
[developer.mend.io/github/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image](https://developer.mend.io/github/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image).
That is why no amount of reading the repo could have found it, and why the
dashboard (issue #8) froze at 2026-07-12 while Renovate kept running.

**Blast radius is wider than the dashboard.** Silent mode also suppressed **two
pending updates** in this single run — `debian 13.6-slim` (digest) and
`mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2025`. Renovate computed them, then
declined to open branches. This is not only a lost alarm; it is a lost update
stream. Note PR #528 was opened 2026-08-06 and this run is 2026-08-07, so silent
mode was switched on inside that window — plausibly a deliberate quieting during
the #529 incident that was never switched back.

**This is a live misconfiguration, not a historical one.** Turning `mode` back to
its default is a settings change on the Mend portal, costs nothing, and restores
both the alarm and the updates.

content.text:
The log answered Open Question 1 — and the answer is bigger than the question.

## `mode=silent` is the root cause, and it's still on

The job log says it in plain text:

```
level 30  Repository is running with mode=silent and will not make Issues or PRs by default
level 20  Dependency Dashboard issue is not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
level 20  Config migration issues are not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
level 20  Branch renovate/debian-13.6-slim creation is disabled because mode=silent
level 20  Branch renovate/mcr.microsoft.com-windows-servercore-ltsc2025 creation is disabled because mode=silent
```

The lookup failure **did** fire in this run — `Failed to look up deb package openjdk-17-jdk-headless: no-result` — and per my earlier trace it was pushed onto `dep.warnings`, destined for the dashboard. Silent mode discarded the delivery. So my previous framing was right that the alarm exists and isn't muted by `suppressNotifications`, but I had the delivery failure as "the dashboard is stale for unknown reasons." It isn't stale — it's switched off.

**Three things follow:**

1. **The blast radius is wider than the alarm.** Silent mode also withheld **two real updates** in this one run: `debian 13.6-slim` (digest) and `windows/servercore:ltsc2025`. Renovate computed them and declined to open branches. You're losing an update stream, not just a warning.

2. **`mode` is set outside the repo.** It's absent from `.github/renovate.json` and from the log's `File config`, `CLI config`, and `Env config` objects — it comes from Mend's per-repository settings. No amount of reading the repo would have found it.

3. **The proposed CI guard would have been silenced too.** A dry-run guard reporting through Renovate's own channels inherits `mode=silent`. Item 2 as specified was going to rebuild an alarm and then hand it the same off-switch.

Timing: PR #528 opened 2026-08-06, this silent run is 2026-08-07 — so it was switched on inside that window, plausibly a deliberate quieting during the #529 incident that never got reverted.

The log also independently confirms PR #531's diagnosis: `getReleases` shows all nine deb lookups hitting the single `suite=stable` URL. But note the caveat — **under `mode=silent`, #531's fix can't be observed end-to-end**, because the resulting PRs won't open.

Findings F1, F6, and F7 stand unchanged. Report updated at `openspec/changes/loud-deb-pin-resolution/research.md`.

The immediate action isn't a change proposal — it's a portal toggle at [developer.mend.io/github/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image](https://developer.mend.io/github/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image), plus a comment on #532 correcting the "debug level only" root cause. Want me to draft that comment?

Here's what I found about Renovate's `mode` config option and silent mode:

## What `mode: "silent"` does

Silent mode is primarily a Mend-hosted app concept, but it's a repository-level config option. When in silent mode, Renovate does not create issues (such as Dependency Dashboard, or due to config errors) or Config Migration PRs, even if enabled. It also does not prune/close any that already exist — even the Dependency Dashboard or Config Warning Issues will stay as-is.

In practice for hosted installs: running in silent mode means no onboarding PR, no dependency updates, and no issues created unless the maintainer proactively creates a `renovate.json`.

## Origin and precedence

The feature came from issue #26724: Silent was defined as the same as `dryRun=lookup`, but also allowing `checkedBranches` to trigger creation of branches/PRs, with pre-existing branches remaining open and updated. Importantly, repo config wins over global/app config: this mode is user-configurable — e.g. if the user configures `mode=remediation` in `renovate.json`, it overrides anything set by the app in global config. `dryRun` still exists and overrides the mode — e.g. with `mode=silent`, `checkedBranches=renovate/foo` and `dryRun=lookup`, no branch is created.

## Opting individual repos out of org-wide silent mode

This is the common use case — install the app org-wide in silent/"Scan Only", then enable specific repos: pick the silent option, and create a `renovate.json` with `mode: 'full'` in the repos you want to go full.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["config:recommended"],
  "mode": "full"
}
```

## Debugging tip

If Renovate is installed and you can see a job log, but it isn't onboarding your repository, look for `dryRun` in the logs to confirm you're in Silent mode. To get an onboarding PR, change to Interactive mode at either the repository or organization level.

One gotcha with inherited config: if you use silent mode, the onboarding config is assumed — but if you have an empty repo config, the `renovate-config` repo settings won't be implicitly included. For that behavior you likely want `inheritConfig`, which is implicit.

**Docs reference:** https://docs.renovatebot.com/mend-hosted/hosted-apps-config/#onboarding-behavior

Here's what the search turned up. Note: I didn't find a **Terraform provider** for managing Mend Renovate repository settings — the results cover Renovate's own `mode: silent` config option and the Mend UI/app settings, plus (separately) Renovate's support for Terraform providers as a dependency type.

## Renovate's `mode: "silent"` settingSetting `"mode": "silent"` makes Renovate scan without creating pull requests, issues, or comments. It is described as a useful trial state for a repository that is onboarded but not yet ready to receive update volume.This configuration option was created primarily for use with Mend's hosted app, but can also be useful for some self-hosted use cases. It enables a `silent` mode allowing repos to be scanned for updates and for users to request such updates be opened in PRs on demand through the Mend UI, without needing the Dependency Dashboard issue in the repo.

 The options `mode=silent` and `dryRun` can be used together.

## How repos end up in silent modeIf you select "All repositories" during installation, new repositories are automatically installed and default to "Silent" mode, and can be independently enabled for Interactive mode. If you choose "Only selected repositories", those selected repositories default to Interactive mode.

In the Mend UI the option is labeled differently: "Scan Only" means repositories will be scanned without checks, issues, and remediation PRs being created, Renovate is set to "silent", and scan results are available in the Developer Platform and Mend App.

## Overriding silent mode per repository

To opt individual repos out: pick the silent option globally and create a `renovate.json` with `mode: 'full'` in the repos you want to go full.

Diagnostics: if Renovate is installed and you can see a job log but it isn't onboarding your repository, look for `dryRun` in the logs to confirm you are in Silent mode, then change to Interactive mode at the Repository or Organization level.

## Caveat on config inheritance

One reported gotcha relevant to Terraform users: grouping Terraform modules into a single PR worked while the repository was configured with Silent mode enabled, but disabling Silent mode reverted to the Renovate default configuration and stopped using the global config repo. The explanation given was that a `renovate-config` repo is proposed in the onboarding config; with silent mode the onboarding config is assumed, but with an empty repo config the `renovate-config` won't be implicitly included.

**If you're actually looking for Terraform IaC management of Renovate settings**, that appears to be unsupported — Mend Renovate settings are managed via the Mend UI or in-repo `renovate.json`. Let me know and I can search specifically for a Mend/Renovate Terraform provider in the registry.

Here's everything the page says about silent mode, plus what it does *not* say:

**On silent mode**

- Org-wide default: "If an Organization installed Renovate with "All repositories" (instead of "Selected repositories"), then Renovate defaults to "Silent" mode (`dryRun=lookup`)."
- Rationale given includes that admins "accidentally onboards hundreds of repositories," and that installing broadly lets "individual repository admins decide if/when to start onboarding."
- Why the name: "It's not just no PRs, it's also no Issues" and it is "a common term across other Mend capabilities."

**How to opt out**

The page describes diagnosis and remedy: "look for `dryRun` in the logs to confirm you are in Silent mode." Then, "To get a onboarding PR from Renovate, change to Interactive mode either at the Repository level or Organization level."

Notably, it doesn't specify where that toggle lives, though the surrounding context (job logs, org/repo settings) points to the Mend Developer Portal rather than a config file.

**Your specific question about `mode` in renovate.json**

The content above contains no `mode` configuration option at all, and says nothing about whether a repo-level config file can override the app's global silent setting. The only repo-file override documented here is for a different setting entirely — fork handling: "To change this behavior, push a `renovate.json` file to the repository with `"forkProcessing": "enabled"`."

So the answer to "does setting `mode` in renovate.json override the global setting?" cannot be determined from this page. Based on what *is* written, the documented escape from silent mode is switching to Interactive mode at the repository or organization level, not a committed config change.

One adjacent detail worth noting: with "Selected repositories" installs, the app "will change `onboardingNoDeps` to `"enabled"`", producing an onboarding PR "even if Renovate does not detect any dependencies" — a different path to the same outcome, decided at install time.

content.text:
That's the authoritative answer, from the issue that introduced the feature.

## No Terraform provider — but there's a better fix

The Terraform Registry API returns **zero** providers for both `mend` and `renovate`:

```
filter[name]=mend      → "total-count": 0
filter[name]=renovate  → "total-count": 0
```

Mend's settings are managed only through the Developer Portal UI. So Terraform can't reach this.

**The good news: you don't need it.** `mode` is a normal repository config option, and repo config *wins* over what the app sets globally. From [renovatebot/renovate#26724](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/26724), the issue that introduced silent mode:

> This mode should be user-configurable, e.g. if the user configures `mode=remediation` in `renovate.json` then it would **override anything set by the app in global config**.

This is the documented escape hatch for exactly your situation — [Mend's docs](https://docs.mend.io/renovate/latest/mend-renovate-cloud) describe the org-wide pattern as "pick the silent option globally and create a `renovate.json` with `mode: 'full'` in the repos you want to go full."

So one line in `.github/renovate.json` does what you wanted Terraform for:

```json
"mode": "full",
```

That's strictly better than IaC-over-the-portal on three counts:

1. **It's in the repo**, so it's version-controlled, code-reviewed, and visible to anyone reading the config — no separate state file or provider to maintain.
2. **It's declarative and self-healing.** If someone flips the portal toggle to Silent again, the next run reads `mode: full` from the repo and overrides it. Terraform would only correct on `apply`; this corrects on every run.
3. **`script/renovate_validate.sh` already validates it** — `renovate-config-validator --strict` will reject a typo'd value, so the guard exists today (though nothing invokes it — see F3 in the research).

One caveat worth flagging before you commit it: there's a [reported gotcha](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/30602) where leaving silent mode changed config inheritance behavior, because silent mode assumes the onboarding config. Your `.github/renovate.json` is fully populated with explicit `extends`, so this shouldn't bite — but it's worth watching the first non-silent run.

This also strengthens the recommendation in the research: Option A stops being "a portal toggle, invisible to code review" and becomes a one-line committed change. That removes the exact weakness I flagged. Want me to fold this into the research file and revise Option A?

content.text:
**Both — but they do different jobs, and only one is the real fix.**

## `mode: "full"` in `.github/renovate.json` — this is the fix

One line. It overrides the portal, it's version-controlled, and it re-asserts itself on **every run**. If the portal gets flipped back to Silent — by you during a future incident, by a Mend default change, by someone else — the repo config wins anyway. That's the durable answer to "so we correct easier when mode silent is enabled again in the future."

## The portal toggle — do it too, but for a different reason

Not as a fix, as an **unblock**. The next Renovate run is the acceptance test for PR #531 (does `getReleases` now list multiple deb `registryUrl`s?), and two updates are currently withheld. Flipping the portal gets you that immediately without waiting for a config PR to merge.

## Why not just one

| | Portal only | renovate.json only | Both |
|---|---|---|---|
| Survives a future re-silencing | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Visible in code review | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Takes effect right now | ✓ | only after merge | ✓ |

Portal-only is what you have today, and it's precisely what failed — an off-switch nobody could see. Config-only works, but you wait for the merge.

## Order

1. Flip the portal to Interactive now — unblocks #531's verification and releases the two held updates.
2. Add `"mode": "full"` to `.github/renovate.json` in the next PR — makes it permanent.

Then watch the first non-silent run for the [config-inheritance gotcha](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/30602) I mentioned. Your config has explicit `extends`, so it should be fine, but it's the one thing that changes when leaving silent mode.

One caveat I should be straight about: I haven't verified that Mend's *hosted* app honors repo-level `mode` in practice. The precedence is stated as design intent in [renovatebot/renovate#26724](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/26724) and matches Mend's documented "set `mode: full` in the repos you want to go full" pattern — but the next job log will confirm it. If the log still says `mode=silent` with the config merged, the portal toggle is doing the work and step 2 is only documentation.

content.text:
**The real config is `mode` in `.github/renovate.json`. The portal UI is not config — it's a default you can override.**

## The layering

Renovate builds one effective config per run by merging layers. Your log shows them by name:

```
File config   ← Mend's infra (token, redis, hostRules)
Env config    ← Mend's app defaults
Repository config  ← .github/renovate.json     ← YOU OWN THIS
```

Repo config is merged last, so it wins. The portal's Silent/Interactive switch is just Mend setting `mode` in a layer *below* yours. Per [renovatebot/renovate#26724](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/26724), the issue that introduced the feature:

> if the user configures `mode=remediation` in `renovate.json` then it would override anything set by the app in global config

So there's no separate "portal setting" to keep in sync. There's one option, `mode`, and two places that can set it — one of which you control and which takes precedence.

## What to add

```json
"mode": "full",
```

Values: `full` (default behavior — PRs, issues, dashboard), `silent` (scan only), `remediation` (security fixes only).

## Why this is the right layer

Your incident is the argument. `mode=silent` was invisible to every form of inspection the repo supports — not in `.github/renovate.json`, not in git history, not in code review. I only found it because you handed me a job log. Any setting that can break your dependency updates and cannot be seen in the repository is in the wrong layer.

Stating it in `renovate.json` moves it into the layer where the rest of your Renovate behavior already lives, and makes the portal irrelevant to it. That's the same reasoning behind PR #531 removing the `suite=` annotation — a field that looks like it steers behavior but doesn't is worse than no field. Here it's the inverse: a field that steers behavior but appears nowhere.

## So: touch the UI or not?

Not necessary, and not where the decision belongs. Once `mode: "full"` is committed, the portal switch stops mattering for this repo — flip it or don't, the repo config overrides it either way. The only reason to touch it is impatience (effect before merge), which you've said you don't care about.

One honest caveat: I've verified the precedence as *stated design intent* and as Mend's own documented "set `mode: full` in the repos you want to go full" pattern, but not empirically against Mend's hosted app. The next job log settles it — if it still reports `mode=silent` after the config merges, then Mend's app is forcing the value and the portal is the only lever. I'd commit the config and check that log line.
