content.text:
The rest of the research, briefly.

## Things that are just wrong right now

**`script/renovate_validate.sh` is invoked by nothing.** Zero call sites across all workflows, `mise.toml`, and scripts. Its only "invocations" are `- [x]` checkboxes in change docs — including PR #531's. `.github/renovate.json` is the only significant config file with no automated verification, while `config/version.json` has three mechanisms and `.github/gx.toml` has `gx lint` + `gx tidy`.

**`JAVA_HOME` is hand-typed and guarded by nothing.** `android.Dockerfile:140` hardcodes `java-17-openjdk-amd64`, two lines from the pin, with no link to it or to `config/version.json`. TODOs at `:136-138` show you already know, blocked on moby/moby#29110.

**`config/version.json`'s `android.java` points backwards.** `update-version.yml:296-303` derives it by running `script/java_version.sh` *inside the previously-published image* — so it describes the last build, not the next one, and lags a cycle by construction. It also feeds nothing user-visible: `readme.md` never mentions Java (grepped), so it only drives the `test/android.yml` self-assertion.

## The openjdk-21 question, corrected

Migration is still worth doing, but **not for the reason the issue gives**. `openjdk-21-jdk-headless` has the *identical* strict-equality sibling (`Depends: openjdk-21-jre-headless (= 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2)`). What it actually removes is the *governance gap* — pin and sibling landing in the same suite set, so they advance together. That deletes `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources`, the COPY/rm pair, the bookworm packageRule, and its load-bearing ordering constraint. AGP 9.0.1 + Gradle 9.1.0 clear the JDK 21 floors comfortably; nothing in the repo declares a JDK constraint at all.

## The structural finding

**"Which Debian release this image is built on" is stated ~21 times across 4 files and defined nowhere.** `config/schema.cue:41-57` models Flutter, Android, Fastlane, and the Windows toolchain — no Debian concept exists. Three of those 21 sites are substrings inside version literals (`+deb13u4`), which no rename can safely touch. This is why scoping the 17→21 migration was expensive while doing it is five edits.

Related: PR #531 introduces a new eye-checkable duplication — `debian_12_bookworm.sources` and its `registryUrls` now restate the same suites/components, which its own `design.md:66` acknowledges. That's the state seam 4 was in for ten weeks. The openjdk-21 migration deletes it.

## Upstream

The `{{#if release }}` typo was **inherited from [Renovate's own deb docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/deb/)**, which document only `suite`/`components`/`binaryArch` — no `release` parameter — yet ship that exact example. Worth a docs PR.

## What I'd do

`mode: full` fixes detection. The openjdk-21 migration is the highest-value next change: it collapses two suite sets into one and makes the leftover hermetic check nearly trivial. Fix `JAVA_HOME` in that same change — a migration is exactly when an unguarded hand-typed path breaks.

Full detail with citations is in `openspec/changes/loud-deb-pin-resolution/research.md`. Want me to fold the `mode: full` conclusion into it and revise Option A?

content.text:
**Root cause of #532:** the `{{#if release }}` template branched on a variable the regex never captured, so all 9 pins resolved against `suite=stable` instead of their real suites. Fixed by PR #531.

**Why nobody noticed for 10 weeks:** `mode=silent` suppressed the Dependency Dashboard, where Renovate's lookup-failure warning would have appeared. Fixed by `mode: full`.

Everything else found:

1. **`script/renovate_validate.sh` is never run** — zero call sites; only `- [x]` checkboxes in docs. So `renovate.json` has no automated check.

2. **`JAVA_HOME` is hand-typed** (`android.Dockerfile:140`) — hardcodes `java-17`, nothing verifies it matches the pin two lines above.

3. **`config/version.json`'s `android.java` is derived backwards** — read from the *previously published* image, so it always lags one cycle. Feeds nothing user-visible.

4. **openjdk-21 has the same strict-sibling constraint as 17** — the issue's stated benefit is wrong. Real benefit: one suite set instead of two, which deletes the bookworm sources file, the COPY/rm, and the special-case rule.

5. **The Debian codename is written ~21 times and defined nowhere** — that's why scoping the 17→21 migration was hard, even though doing it is 5 edits.

6. **PR #531 adds a new eye-checkable duplication** — `debian_12_bookworm.sources` and its `registryUrls` restate the same suites. The openjdk-21 migration deletes it.

7. **The typo came from Renovate's own docs** — their deb example ships the same broken `{{#if release }}`. Worth an upstream PR.

**Suggested order:** `mode: full` → openjdk-21 migration (fix `JAVA_HOME` in it) → decide if items 1–3 are worth guarding.

// Snippet to include at the end of android/app/build.gradle.kts

tasks.register<DefaultTask>("updateAndroidVersions") {
    doLast {
        val jsonFile = File("../../config/version.json")     

        // Parse existing JSON file
        val resultJsonMap = groovy.json.JsonSlurper().parseText(jsonFile.readText()) as MutableMap<String, Any>

        // Get unique platform versions
        val platformVersions = listOf(
            flutter.targetSdkVersion,
            flutter.compileSdkVersion
        ).distinct()

        // Read the build-tools version that AGP will request at build time
        // (AGP's bundled default unless the Flutter template overrides it). This
        // is the only value that's guaranteed to match what sdkmanager installs
        // for `flutter create test_app && ./gradlew bundleRelease`.
        // Flutter 3.44 still sets android.newDsl=false (AppExtension); future
        // versions will flip to the new DSL (ApplicationExtension). Try both.
        val buildToolsVersion: String = project.extensions
            .findByType(com.android.build.api.dsl.ApplicationExtension::class.java)
            ?.buildToolsVersion
            ?: project.extensions
                .findByType(com.android.build.gradle.AppExtension::class.java)
                ?.buildToolsVersion
            ?: error("Could not resolve buildToolsVersion from the AGP extension on project ${project.path}")

        // Create new Android version data
        val newJsonMap = mapOf(
            "platforms" to platformVersions.map {
                mapOf("version" to it)
            },
            "gradle" to mapOf("version" to gradle.gradleVersion),
            "buildTools" to mapOf("version" to buildToolsVersion),
            "ndk" to mapOf("version" to flutter.ndkVersion)
        )

        // Merge new values into the existing JSON structure
        (resultJsonMap["android"] as? MutableMap<String, Any>)?.putAll(newJsonMap)

        // Format JSON with pretty printing
        val jsonStr = groovy.json.JsonOutput.toJson(resultJsonMap)
        val prettyStr = groovy.json.JsonOutput.prettyPrint(jsonStr)
        
        println(prettyStr)

        // Write updated JSON back to the file
        jsonFile.writeText("$prettyStr\n")
    }
}

content.text:
Your link is a **floor, not a target** — and there's no ceiling. Let me answer everything.

## Your question first: does Flutter support Java 21?

**Yes.** The constants you linked are minimums:

```kotlin
warnJavaVersion  = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
errorJavaVersion = JavaVersion.VERSION_17
```

`checkJavaVersion` only tests **downward** — it errors when `version < 17`, warns when `version < 17`. Nothing checks whether a JDK is too new. The test file confirms: 17 passes, 16 throws, and a comment says there's no warn-tier because *"the lowest supported Java version is also the lowest possible."*

So 17 is Flutter's **floor**. Your image currently ships exactly the minimum. **Java 21 is supported** — and your AGP 9.0.1 / Gradle 9.1.0 clear its floors too.

That reframes the migration: it's not "17 is what Flutter supports," it's "17 is the oldest Flutter tolerates, and we're paying an entire extra Debian suite to stay there."

---

## 1. Does Renovate validate automatically?

**No.** The GitHub App does not validate config on branches. Renovate validates only when *it* runs (weekly schedule), and a bad config surfaces as a Config Warning issue — which `mode=silent` was suppressing.

**Simplest fix:** add the existing script to `build.yml`'s meta lane, which already has three hermetic ~10s jobs:

```yaml
- run: script/renovate_validate.sh
```

Zero new tooling — the script exists, nothing calls it. Bonus: it validates `mode: "full"` too.

## 2 + 3. Java version: read it from where?

Your instinct is right and there's a better source than either the image or the Dockerfile. Flutter publishes it in `gradle_utils.dart` (the checker says Java values *"should align with"* it) — but that's a floor, so tracking it would pin you to the minimum forever.

**Best UX + lowest maintenance: delete the concept.** Today Java is 5 representations across 3 mechanisms, and `config/version.json.android.java` feeds *nothing user-visible* (readme never mentions Java). The `script/java_version.sh` derivation reads the *previous* image, so it always lags a cycle.

Simplest long-term: keep the pin as the single source of truth, derive `JAVA_HOME` and the manifest *from it* rather than the reverse. That kills the backwards derivation, the unguarded `JAVA_HOME`, and the one-cycle lag in one move.

## 4. What I meant

`config/version.json` says `"java": {"version": 17}` — but that number is *measured from the last published image*, not *declared for the next one*. Edit it to 21 and nothing changes about what gets installed. It's a mirror labelled as a dial.

## 5. Debian DevEx

The codename is written ~21 times across 4 files and defined nowhere — `config/schema.cue` models Flutter/Android/Fastlane/Windows but has no Debian concept.

**Simplest fix is the openjdk-21 migration itself.** It deletes 9 of those 21 sites (the whole bookworm half). What remains is one base image digest plus `+deb13u` suffixes inside version strings that Renovate maintains anyway. No new schema, no generator — just fewer places.

## 6. What I meant

PR #531 has `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` and `renovate.json`'s `registryUrls` both listing the same suites/components. Two files stating one fact, cross-checked by nothing — its own design.md calls it *"checkable by eye,"* which is what seam 4 was for ten weeks. Migrating to 21 deletes both.

## 7. Upstream

Noted — no upstream PR. I'll add a comment to PR #531 recording that the `{{#if release }}` example came from Renovate's own deb docs.

---

## Proposal

| # | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `"mode": "full"` in renovate.json | Restores the alarm; survives portal re-silencing |
| 2 | `script/renovate_validate.sh` into `build.yml` | Script exists, nothing calls it; ~10s hermetic |
| 3 | **openjdk 17 → 21** | Deletes the bookworm suite, the sources file, the special-case rule, the eye-check duplication, and 9 codename sites. Flutter supports it. |
| 4 | Derive `JAVA_HOME` + manifest from the pin | Kills the unguarded hardcode and the backwards derivation |

1 and 2 are one small PR. 3 and 4 belong together — a migration is exactly when an unguarded hand-typed path breaks.

Want me to write these into the research file and draft the proposals?

Here's what the search turned up on Renovate's reconfigure branch and how it relates to `branchPrefix` and config migration:

## The reconfigure branch patternRenovate can validate configuration changes in Pull Requests when you use a special branch name. Create a new Git branch that matches the `{{branchPrefix}}reconfigure` pattern — for example, with the default prefix `renovate/`, the branch name must be `renovate/reconfigure`. Then commit your updated Renovate config file to that branch and push it to your Git hosting platform.

On the next run, Renovate will search for a branch matching the special reconfigure pattern, check for a config file in the reconfigure branch (it can even find a renamed configuration file compared to the one on the default branch), and add a passing or failing status to the branch depending on the outcome of the config validation run. On the Mend-hosted apps, if there's a PR, Renovate will add comments to it.

This feature was added in Renovate 37.44.0.

## Relationship to branchPrefix

The reconfigure branch name is derived from `branchPrefix`, so if you customize it the branch changes too. For example, if you want branches like `deps/eslint-4.x` instead of `renovate/eslint-4.x`, you set `branchPrefix = deps/`; or use `renovate_` if you want to avoid forward slashes. In that case your reconfigure branch would be `deps/reconfigure` or `renovate_reconfigure`.

Note the contrast with the **onboarding** branch, which is *not* templated from `branchPrefix`: this setting is independent of branchPrefix — if you configure branchPrefix to be `renovate-`, you'd still get the onboarding PR created with branch `renovate/configure` until you configure `onboardingBranch=renovate-configure` or similar.

## Important caveat: reconfigure does not run config migration

A known gotcha is that validation on the reconfigure branch behaves differently from the standalone config validator: you may get no error from `config-validator` because it migrates the config before validating (e.g. `regexManagers` migrated to `customManagers`), whereas the reconfigure logic doesn't perform the migration. So legacy option names can fail validation on `renovate/reconfigure` while passing elsewhere.

Also useful when iterating: Renovate skips the PR/branch if there is an existing status-check, so adding a new commit to the branch could fix the issue (i.e. re-trigger validation).

## Config migration as a separate mechanism

Config migration is its own feature, distinct from the reconfigure branch. It works by migrating legacy config internally before the config is used; when done right it "just works" silently and legacy configs keep working indefinitely, with the only sign being a debug message in the logs noting the old and newly migrated configs. Renovate can also create a config migration Pull Request to migrate legacy config in your configuration file — set `configMigration` to `true`, as config migration PRs are disabled by default. Self-hosted users can combine `migratePresets` with `configMigration` to have presets migrated by PR.

Sources: [Config Validation](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-validation/), [Configuration Options](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/), [Config Migration](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-migration/), [Config Template Editing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-templates/)

It also carries a staleness disclaimer ("We don't, in general, keep these breaking change docs up to date").

The one thing docs do state authoritatively is **resolution order**:

final warnJavaMinVersionAndroid = Version(17, 0, 0);

// versions that we support.
// Source of truth: https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/compatibility.html
const oneMajorVersionHigherJavaVersion = '26';
```

Note the naming: `errorJavaMin…`/`warnJavaMin…` — explicitly **minimums**. |---|---|---|

## Config Validation

You can check your Renovate configuration with a standalone program called `renovate-config-validator`. All [`renovate` distributions](https://docs.renovatebot.com/getting-started/running/#available-distributions) include this program.

## Default behavior

When you run `renovate-config-validator` with no arguments it will check:

- all [default locations](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/) (if files exist)
- the `RENOVATE_CONFIG_FILE` environment variable

For example:

```
$ npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator
 INFO: Validating renovate.json
 INFO: Config validated successfully
```

If you want to run `renovate-config-validator` while using a custom filename for your renovate config file, you will need to pass the filename as cli argument.

### Strict mode

By default, the validator program fails with a non-zero exit code if there are any validation warnings or errors. You can pass the `--strict` flag to make it fail if a scanned config needs migration:

```
$ npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator --strict
 INFO: Validating renovate.json
 WARN: Config migration necessary
       "oldConfig": {
         "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
         "extends": [ "config:base" ]
       },
       "newConfig": {
         "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
         "extends": [ "config:recommended" ]
       },
```

### Pass file to check as CLI arguments

You can pass the file you want to check to the `renovate-config-validator` program with a CLI argument. This can be handy to check a config file with a non-default name, like when you're using preset repositories. For example:

```
$ npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator first_config.json
 INFO: Validating first_config_.json
 INFO: Config validated successfully
```

> [!note] Note
> If you specify the filename, `renovate-config-validator` treats the file(s) as global self-hosted configuration instead of repo-level configuration. If this isn't intentional - for instance if you're validating a [shared config preset](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-presets/) or a non-standard filename - make sure you specify `--no-global`, i.e. `renovate-config-validator --no-global go-presets.json`.

### Providing global configuration

If `renovate-config-validator` detects a `config.js`, or any [global self-hosed environment variables](https://docs.renovatebot.com/self-hosted-configuration/), they will be set as global configuration.

For instance, if you had a `config.js`:

```
module.exports = {
  // to mirror the Mend-hosted Renovate
  globalExtends: ['global:safeEnv'],
};
```

And a `renovate.json`:

```
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "env": {
    "GONOSUMDB": "off"
  }
}
```

The `renovate-config-validator` would allow this to pass.

## Validate your config automatically

You can create a [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/) hook to validate your configuration automatically. Go to the [`renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks` repository](https://github.com/renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks) for more information.

### Validation of Renovate config change PRs

> [!tip] Tip
> Using the Mend-hosted apps? Push a branch to `renovate/reconfigure` for feedback (via status check), and if there's a PR, Renovate will add comments to it!

Renovate can validate configuration changes in Pull Requests when you use a special branch name.

Follow these steps to validate your configuration:

1. Create a new Git branch that matches the `{{branchPrefix}}reconfigure` pattern. For example, if you're using the default prefix `renovate/`, your branch name must be `renovate/reconfigure`.
2. Commit your updated Renovate config file to this branch, and push it to your Git hosting platform.

The next time Renovate runs on that repo it will:

1. Search for a branch that matches the special reconfigure pattern.
2. Check for a config file in the reconfigure branch. Renovate can even find a renamed configuration file (compared to the config file in the default branch).
3. Add a passing or failing status to the branch, depending on the outcome of the config validation run.
4. If there's an *open* pull request with validation errors from the *reconfigure* branch then Renovate comments in the PR with details.
5. Validate each commit the next time Renovate runs on the repository, until the PR is merged.

> [!note] Note
> The reconfigure branch **must** be pushed to the source repository that Renovate runs against, not a fork.

3. Add a passing or failing status to the branch, depending on the outcome of the config validation run.
4. If there's an *open* pull request with validation errors from the *reconfigure* branch then Renovate comments in the PR with details.
5. Validate each commit the next time Renovate runs on the repository, until the PR is merged.

> [!note] Note
> The reconfigure branch **must** be pushed to the source repository that Renovate runs against, not a fork.

content.text:
Both answered — and each has a finding that changes the plan.

## Java extraction: the honest answer

**No Flutter source publishes a "recommended JDK for users."** There are three different things, and they disagree:

| Source | Value | What it actually means |
|---|---|---|
| `DependencyVersionChecker.kt` / `gradle_utils.dart` | 17 | **Floor** — errors below |
| `flutter create` template | **17** | What scaffolded apps compile against |
| Flutter's `DEPS` | 21 | **Flutter's own engine CI JDK** — for running the formatter |

I have to correct myself: I called 21 "de-facto blessed" based on `DEPS`. That was wrong. The `DEPS` comment says the JDK is fetched *"since java is required for running the formatter"* — it's Flutter's internal build tooling, not a recommendation to users. **The template — what Flutter actually scaffolds for users — declares 17.**

So: **automatic extraction gives you 17, not 21.** Java 21 has no upstream justification. It would be your judgment call, deliberately diverging from what extraction reports.

The two are in tension, and you should pick one:
- **Extraction (17)** — self-maintaining, tracks Flutter, but keeps bookworm and the whole special case.
- **Java 21** — deletes bookworm, but is a maintainer choice no upstream source backs, and it needs documenting as such.

**Best extraction mechanism** — extend the Gradle task you already have, matching `updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts`'s "interrogate the live toolchain" pattern:

```kotlin
val javaVersion: String = project.extensions
    .findByType(com.android.build.api.dsl.ApplicationExtension::class.java)
    ?.compileOptions?.sourceCompatibility?.majorVersion
    ?: project.extensions
        .findByType(com.android.build.gradle.AppExtension::class.java)
        ?.compileOptions?.sourceCompatibility?.majorVersion
    ?: error("Could not resolve sourceCompatibility from the AGP extension on ${project.path}")
```

Zero new fetches, reuses your dual-DSL fallback, fails loudly. Rejected alternatives: `flutter doctor` is circular (reports the *installed* JDK — reproduces today's bug); `flutter analyze --suggestions` is explicitly excluded from `--machine` output (`machineOutput => false`) and returns a verdict, never a version; `releases_linux.json` has no Java key.

## Enforcing `renovate/reconfigure`

Bad news on enforcement: it's a **convention, not a gate**. From the [docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-validation/), validation only happens *"the next time Renovate runs on that repo"* — your weekly schedule. Nothing forces the branch name, and the status arrives too late to block a PR.

Since you want enforcement, the reliable option is CI — and it's cheap because the script already exists:

```yaml
# build.yml, alongside validate-version-files
- run: script/renovate_validate.sh
```

Add `paths: ['.github/renovate.json']` so it only runs when relevant. That's a real required check on every PR, ~10s, no egress. Use `renovate/reconfigure` *additionally* when you want Renovate's own richer feedback on a config change — but don't rely on it as the gate.

Note one caveat if you do both: reconfigure **doesn't run config migration first**, so legacy option names can fail there while passing `--strict`.

## Where this leaves the proposal

The Java decision now needs you:

- **A — Extract (17):** fully connected, self-maintaining, no upstream divergence. Keeps bookworm, the special-case rule, and the eye-check duplication.
- **B — Extract *and* pin 21:** deletes bookworm; extraction becomes a *floor check* (assert shipped ≥ template) rather than the source of truth. More moving parts, documented as a deliberate choice.

I'd lean **B** — the extraction still earns its keep as a guard, and 21 is what Flutter's own toolchain uses and where users land via Android Studio. But it is a divergence from upstream, and A is the defensible "follow Flutter" reading you originally asked for.

## 1. Yes — the snippet reads exactly what `flutter create` produced

Let me be precise about the mechanism, because it's the crux of the design.

`updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts` isn't parsing Flutter's source. It's appended to a **real app created by `flutter create`**, then run as a Gradle task. So it reads the *live, resolved* configuration of a scaffolded Flutter app:

```
flutter create test_app          ← Flutter scaffolds from its template
        │
        ▼
android/app/build.gradle.kts     ← template output: compileOptions { sourceCompatibility = VERSION_17 }
        │
        ▼
Gradle configures the project    ← AGP extension now holds the resolved value
        │
        ▼
updateAndroidVersions task ──▶ reads compileOptions.sourceCompatibility ──▶ "17"
```

So it answers *"what Java version does a real Flutter app declare?"* — which is the same question as "what does `flutter create` do," just asked of the built object rather than the template text. Same source you'd use for `ndkVersion` and `buildToolsVersion` today.

**The alternative** would be grepping the template file in the image:
`$FLUTTER_ROOT/packages/flutter_tools/templates/app/android-kotlin.tmpl/app/build.gradle.kts.tmpl` for `VERSION_(\d+)`. Same value today, but regex-on-source, and there are three templates (`android-kotlin`, `android-java`, `plugin/android-kotlin`) that could diverge.

Reading the AGP extension is better: it's an API, it's the value AGP actually compiles with, and it fails loudly if the shape changes.

### So the design settles cleanly

**Java 17 it is.** That means:

- `config/version.json` `android.java.version` becomes a **real derivation** from the Flutter version being built — same mechanism, same job, same file as `gradle`/`buildTools`/`ndk`.
- The backwards `script/java_version.sh` step disappears, and with it the one-cycle lag.
- `JAVA_HOME` and the Dockerfile pin derive from that value instead of floating free.
- **openjdk-21 is off the table** — no upstream basis. Bookworm stays.

Which means items 5 and 6 from my earlier list (Debian codename sprawl, PR #531's eye-check duplication) don't get deleted by a migration. They stay as-is, or get addressed on their own merits later. I'd leave them: they're real but not urgent, and the `mode: full` fix removes the silence that made them dangerous.

One thing worth naming in the design: the extraction gives a **floor-aligned** value. If Flutter ever raises the template to 21, you'd inherit it automatically — which is exactly the property you want, and the reason to build this rather than hand-bump.

Two open design questions before implementation:

- **Does the pin follow automatically, or does it gate?** `version.json` can be derived, but `ARG OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION` has the major version welded into its *name* — a 17→21 move is a rename plus a suite change, not a value bump. Cleanest is to derive `version.json`, and have CI **fail loudly** if the shipped major diverges from it, leaving the actual migration a deliberate human change.
- **Does the readme show Java?** It currently never mentions it. Once `version.json` is a real declaration, publishing it is nearly free.

## 2. Enforcing `renovate/reconfigure` in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md

Proposed rule — concise, no jargon, no history:

```markdown
## Renovate config changes

Changes to `.github/renovate.json` go on a branch named `renovate/reconfigure`.
Renovate validates that branch and reports the result on the PR.
```

Two notes on scope, so you can decide:

- This binds **agents**, not humans or the tooling. It's a convention with a reminder, not a gate. If you want it actually enforced, that's the CI job (`script/renovate_validate.sh` in `build.yml`, filtered to `paths: ['.github/renovate.json']`).
- Renovate only validates the branch when it next runs — on your weekly schedule — so feedback isn't immediate.

Want me to write the design into `research.md` and draft the rule into both files? Note that adding the rule is an edit to tracked files, so I'd want your go-ahead — and it's outside explore mode's read-only scope, so it may be cleaner as a small change proposal.

**Continue #531 — it's still the right fix, and Java 17 makes it *more* necessary, not less.**

It's clean, mergeable, up to date with main, 12 checks green.

The reasoning: #531 fixes a bug that exists independently of the Java decision. All nine pins resolve against `suite=stable`, which follows whatever Debian calls stable. That's live today and would silently retarget every pin when Debian 14 ships.

And the Java 17 decision **removes the escape hatch**. Earlier the openjdk-21 migration would have deleted the bookworm pin, making #531's special-case rule moot. Now bookworm stays permanently, so the cross-suite rule is a permanent requirement — exactly what #531 builds.

One thing to fix before merging. #531's description says:

> **Replacing openjdk-17 with trixie's openjdk-21.** …flagging it for you rather than deciding it here.

That's now decided — against. Worth recording so it doesn't get re-litigated: `flutter create` scaffolds `sourceCompatibility = VERSION_17`, and Flutter's `DEPS` pin to 21 is its engine CI's formatter JDK, not a user recommendation.

Renovate's own channels inherits `mode=silent` too. Before any new guard is
designed, fix the one that was switched off.

**Item 3 → migrate to openjdk-21, but on corrected grounds.** Not because it
removes the strict-sibling hazard (F6: it does not), but because it collapses two
suite sets into one and retires the entire bookworm special case. If it proceeds,
fix `JAVA_HOME` (`android.Dockerfile:140`) in the same change — it is the one
Java representation with no guard at all, and a migration is exactly when an
unguarded hand-typed path breaks.

**Sequencing:** item 3 makes item 2's Option C nearly trivial (one suite set, no
special case, nothing to cross-check at seam 8). If both are wanted, do 3 first.

The deeper structural finding — that "which Debian release this image is built on"
is stated ~21 times across 4 files and *defined nowhere*, while `config/version.json`
models Flutter/Android/Fastlane/Windows but has no Debian concept at all
(`config/schema.cue:41-57`) — is what makes item 3 expensive to *scope* rather
than to *do*. Recommend a separate change; it is not blocking either item here.

`flutter create` scaffolds `VERSION_17` and no upstream source recommends higher.

**PR #531 → continue, do not close.** It is clean, mergeable, and 12 checks green.
Its bug is live and independent of the Java decision: all nine pins resolve against
`suite=stable`, which follows whatever Debian calls stable and would silently
retarget every pin when Debian 14 ships. Staying on 17 makes bookworm permanent, so
#531's cross-suite rule is a permanent requirement rather than a stopgap that a
migration would have deleted. Two edits before merging: strike the "consider
openjdk-21" follow-up (now decided against, with F6's reasoning recorded so it is
not re-litigated), and note that the `{{#if release }}` example came from

(F7) — no upstream PR for now. Its acceptance test cannot be observed until
`mode: full` lands, so sequence that first.

**Enforcing `renovate/reconfigure`.** Renovate validates a branch matching
`{{branchPrefix}}reconfigure` and posts a status to it
([docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-validation/)), but only *"the next time
Renovate runs"* — the weekly schedule. It is a convention, not a gate, and nothing
forces the branch name. Record it as a short rule in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`; if a
hard gate is wanted, that is `script/renovate_validate.sh` in `build.yml` filtered to
`paths: ['.github/renovate.json']`. Caveat if both are used: reconfigure does not run
config migration first, so legacy option names can fail there while passing `--strict`.

Since the openjdk-21 migration is off, two earlier findings no longer get deleted
for free and stand on their own merits, neither urgent: the Debian codename stated
~21 times across 4 files and defined nowhere (`config/schema.cue:41-57` has no
Debian concept), and PR #531's new seam-8 duplication (F4). `mode: full` removes the
silence that made both dangerous.

## Open Questions

1. **Why is `mode=silent` set, and was it intentional?** The log proves *that* it
   is set and that it comes from Mend's per-repository settings (absent from the
   repo config and from the log's `File`/`CLI`/`Env` config objects). Timing —
   PR #528 opened 2026-08-06, silent run 2026-08-07 — suggests it was switched on
   during the #529 incident. Whether that was deliberate, and whether anything
   still depends on it, is a maintainer/portal question not answerable from the
   repo or the log.

2. **Is the JDK the published image offers part of its contract?** `readme.md`
   never mentions Java (grepped), and `config/version.json.android.java` feeds only
   an internal test — so nothing *documents* JDK 17 to users. But downstream
   Flutter/AGP builds consume it at runtime. Maintainer call; not findable in code
   or on the web.

[developer.mend.io/github/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image](https://developer.mend.io/github/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image).

acceptance test and the two withheld updates. Then file a comment on #532
recording F2 — the issue's stated root cause ("debug level only") is wrong, and
the correction matters for anyone reading it later.

  A is a portal toggle, not a change, or
- **`openjdk-21-migration`** — item 3, which shrinks the above.

Recommend proposing the openjdk-21 migration first. Separately, consider an
upstream docs PR to renovatebot/renovate for the `{{#if release}}` example (F7).

attachment.snippet:
1	# Research: making apt-pin resolution failure loud (issue #532, items 2 & 3)
2	
3	Scope: issue #532 item 1 is done (PR #531). This researches the two open items:
4	
5	- **Item 2** — make silent Renovate resolution failure loud.
6	- **Item 3** — decide whether to migrate openjdk-17 → openjdk-21.
7	
8	## Headline
9	
10	**Item 2 is already built — by Renovate, at WARN level, on the Dependency
11	Dashboard. It did not fire because the repository is running with `mode=silent`,
12	which suppresses the dashboard write entirely.** The issue's premise that
13	`no-result` is "logged at debug level only" is incorrect. Building a
14	network-dry-run CI guard would be reimplementing a mechanism the repo already
15	pays for and has switched off.
16	
17	**`mode=silent` is the actual root cause of the ten weeks of silence, and it is
18	still on.** It also suppresses PR creation — two updates were withheld in the
19	2026-08-07 run alone. This outranks both items in the issue.
20	
21	**Item 3 is decided: stay on openjdk-17. Do not migrate.** `flutter create`
22	scaffolds `sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17`, and no Flutter source
23	publishes a recommended JDK above that floor. Flutter's `DEPS` pin to JDK 21 is
24	its *engine CI's* JDK ("required for running the formatter") — not a user-facing
25	recommendation. See F6. Bookworm therefore stays permanently, which makes PR #531
26	a permanent requirement rather than a stopgap.
27	
28	**The replacement for item 3: derive the Java version from Flutter instead of
29	hand-maintaining it.** `config/version.json`'s `android.java.version` is currently
30	measured from the *previously published image*; it should be derived from the
31	Flutter version being built, like `gradle`/`buildTools`/`ndk` already are. See F6b.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Context
36	
37	What exists today, after PR #531 lands.
38	
39	```
40	  android.Dockerfile                    .github/renovate.json
41	  ┌──────────────────────────┐          ┌─────────────────────────────┐
42	  │ # renovate: depName=curl │─────────▶│ customManagers[1]           │
43	  │ ARG CURL_VERSION="…"     │  regex   │   matchStrings              │
44	  │        × 9 pins          │          │   datasourceTemplate: deb   │
45	  └──────────────────────────┘          │                             │
46	                                        │ packageRules                │
47	  config/debian_12_bookworm.sources     │  ├─ deb → trixie ×3   (main)│
48	  ┌──────────────────────────┐          │  └─ openjdk-17 → bookworm ×3│
49	  │ Suites: bookworm …       │◀ ─ ─ ─ ─▶│       (4 components)        │
50	  │ Components: main contrib…│  "checkable  └─────────────────────────┘
51	  └──────────────────────────┘   by eye"              │
52	                                                      ▼
53	                                              deb.debian.org
54	```
55	
56	Nine pins, all in `android.Dockerfile`: `curl:8`, `git:10`, `lcov:12`,
57	`ca-certificates:14`, `unzip:16`, `ruby-full:97`, `build-essential:99`,
58	`openjdk-17-jdk-headless:144`, `sudo:146`. Eight resolve against trixie; one
59	against bookworm, added solely because trixie has no openjdk-17
60	(`android.Dockerfile:149`).
61	
62	The verification surface (11 workflows). `build.yml:372-444` holds three
63	hermetic, ~10s, no-`needs:` config jobs — `validate-version-files` (`cue vet`),
64	`validate-generated-config` (`update_test.sh` + `git diff --exit-code`),
65	`build-docs`. This is the repo's meta lane and its one verification idiom:
66	**commit two representations of a fact and diff them in CI** (used at
67	`build.yml:412-414`, `update-docs.yml:49-57`, `gx.yml:78-93`).
68	
69	`script/renovate_validate.sh` runs `renovate-config-validator --strict`. It is
70	invoked by **nothing** — grep across all workflows, `mise.toml` and scripts
71	returns zero call sites. Its only references are `- [x]` checkboxes in change
72	documents (`openspec/changes/archive/2026-06-08-fix-renovate-dockerfile-pins/tasks.md:4`,
73	and PR #531's `tasks.md:23`). `.github/renovate.json` is the only significant
74	config file in the repo with no automated verification.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Findings
79	
80	### F1 — Renovate already surfaces this at WARN, on the dashboard
81	
82	Traced through Renovate's source:
83	
84	1. Lookup fails → `res.warnings.push({topic, message: 'Failed to look up deb package X: no-result'})`
85	   — `lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/index.ts:291-303`. The `logger.debug`
86	   at :295 that the issue cites is *adjacent to*, not instead of, the warnings push.
87	2. `getDepWarnings()` collects every `dep.warnings` and calls
88	   **`logger.warn({warnings, files}, 'Package lookup failures')`** —
89	   `lib/workers/repository/errors-warnings.ts:59-61`. **WARN, not debug.**
90	3. `getDepWarningsDashboard()` renders "⚠️ **Warning** Renovate failed to look up
91	   the following dependencies: … Files affected: …" — `errors-warnings.ts:112-138`.
92	4. It is written into the dashboard issue body at
93	   `lib/workers/repository/dependency-dashboard.ts:563-567`.
94	
95	The only gate is `config.suppressNotifications?.includes('dependencyLookupWarnings')`
96	(`errors-warnings.ts:116`). **`.github/renovate.json` sets no `suppressNotifications`.**
97	Third-party dashboards confirm the rendered form in the wild, `no-result` included
98	— e.g. [trueforge-org/truecharts#18710](https://github.com/trueforge-org/truecharts/issues/18710).
99	
100	So the correct-by-construction alarm existed the whole time and was not muted.
101	
102	### F2 — Root cause: the repository is running with `mode=silent`
103	
104	**Confirmed from the Mend job log** (`gmeligio_flutter-docker-image_2026-08-07_14-50_019fdc2a…log`,
105	Renovate 44.12.0, 173 lines). The log contains, verbatim:
106	
107	```
108	level 30  Repository is running with mode=silent and will not make Issues or PRs by default
109	level 20  Silent mode enabled so repo is considered onboarded
110	level 20  Dependency Dashboard issue is not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
111	level 20  Config migration issues are not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
112	level 20  Branch renovate/debian-13.6-slim creation is disabled because mode=silent
113	level 20  Branch renovate/mcr.microsoft.com-windows-servercore-ltsc2025 creation is disabled because mode=silent
114	```
115	
116	The lookup failure **did** occur in this run —
117	`Failed to look up deb package openjdk-17-jdk-headless: no-result` — and per F1 it
118	was pushed onto `dep.warnings`, destined for the dashboard. Silent mode discarded
119	the delivery.
120	
121	```
122	  F1: the alarm fires ────────────────────────────┐
123	                                                  │
124	  lookup fails → dep.warnings → getDepWarnings()  │  logger.warn ✓
125	                       │                          │
126	                       ▼                          │
127	             getDepWarningsDashboard()            │
128	                       │                          │
129	                       ▼                          │
130	             dependency-dashboard.ts:563 ─────────┤
131	                       │                          │
132	                       ▼                          │
133	             ✗ mode=silent — issue not written ◀──┘  THE SILENCE
134	```
135	
136	Corroborating detail: the log's own level histogram is **168 debug / 6 info /
137	zero WARN**. The `logger.warn('Package lookup failures')` at
138	`errors-warnings.ts:59-61` does not appear — consistent with the log being
139	captured at a level that elides it, or with silent mode short-circuiting before
140	the aggregation. Either way the operator-facing signal is absent from the log too,
141	so *neither* channel (dashboard nor log warning) carried it.
142	
143	`mode` is set **outside the repository**. It is absent from `.github/renovate.json`,

## Should you continue #531?

**Continue it.** It's clean, mergeable, up to date with main, 12 checks green.

Two reasons the Java decision *strengthens* it rather than weakening it:

1. **Its bug is live and independent.** All nine pins resolve against `suite=stable`, which follows whatever Debian calls stable. When Debian 14 ships, all nine silently retarget — the exact mechanism that broke you when trixie replaced bookworm.

2. **Staying on 17 makes bookworm permanent.** Earlier, the openjdk-21 migration would have deleted the bookworm pin and made #531's special-case rule moot. Now it's a permanent requirement.

Two edits before merging:
- Strike the "consider openjdk-21" follow-up — now decided against, with the reasoning recorded so it isn't re-litigated.
- Add the note you asked for: the `{{#if release }}` example came from Renovate's own deb docs. No upstream PR.

And its acceptance test can't be observed until `mode: full` lands, so sequence that first.

## What changed in research.md

- **Headline** now leads with the two settled decisions: stay on 17, derive the version.
- **F6** rewritten with the three-source table — floor (17), template (**17**), and Flutter's `DEPS` (21, its *engine CI formatter* JDK). I explicitly recorded my earlier "de-facto blessed" reading as a correction, since it was wrong and it drove the previous recommendation.
- **F6b** (new) — the derivation design: the `flutter create` → Gradle → AGP-extension chain, plus the four rejected candidates with reasons.
- **F7** — Java's five representations and which are guarded (`JAVA_HOME`: nothing).
- **Recommendation** — #531 continue-not-close, and the `renovate/reconfigure` enforcement caveat.
- **Open Questions** now includes the one thing I haven't verified: whether Mend's hosted app actually honours repo-level `mode`. It's design intent from [#26724](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/26724), and the next job log settles it.

## Sequence

| # | Change |
|---|---|
| 1 | `"mode": "full"` → branch `renovate/reconfigure` |
| 2 | Merge #531 (after the two edits) |
| 3 | Java derivation + delete `java_version.sh` + fix `JAVA_HOME` |

Step 3 is the substantive one and wants a proper design pass — mainly the open question of whether the Dockerfile pin *follows* the derived value or just *gates* on it, since the major version is welded into the ARG name.

Tracking issue so this is followable independently of the PRs. Sequel to #486, which was the same *class* of bug (a Renovate misconfiguration that silently stopped maintaining the Debian pins) with a different cause.

> **Updated 2026-08-08 after reading the Mend job log.** Two of this issue's original claims were wrong: the `no-result` is *not* debug-only, and the openjdk-21 migration is *not* warranted. Both are corrected below. The original text is preserved in the collapsed section at the bottom.

## What happened

CI on `main` broke in [run 31078705754](https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/actions/runs/31078705754). The `android` stage failed at `android.Dockerfile:151`:

```
openjdk-17-jdk-headless : Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= 17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2)
                          but 17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1 is to be installed
E: Unable to correct problems, you have held broken packages.
```

`openjdk-17-jdk-headless` carries a strict `Depends: openjdk-17-jre-headless (= <same version>)`. Only the JDK is pinned. Debian published `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1`, which became apt's candidate for the JRE while the JDK stayed pinned at `17.0.19+10-1~deb12u2`, so apt could not satisfy the equality constraint. Fixed by hand in #529.

## Root causes

There are **two**, and they are independent. The first explains why the pin went stale; the second explains why nobody found out for ten weeks.

### 1. Resolution — every pin resolved against the wrong suite

The `registryUrlTemplate` in `.github/renovate.json` branches on `{{#if release }}`, but `matchStrings` captures a group named **`suite`**, never `release`. The conditional therefore always falls through to the hard-coded `suite=stable` else-branch. The 2026-08-07 job log confirms all nine apt pins resolving to **one** registry URL:

```json
"deb": { "registryUrls": {
  "https://deb.debian.org/debian?suite=stable&components=main,contrib,non-free&binaryArch=amd64": { "stats": { "count": 9 } }
}}
```

Since Debian 13 trixie became stable, the eight `suite=trixie` pins kept working **by coincidence**, while the single `suite=bookworm` pin resolved against a suite that does not ship `openjdk-17`:

```
"Failed to look up deb package openjdk-17-jdk-headless: no-result"
```

`suite=stable` follows whatever Debian currently calls stable, so this is latent for **all nine pins**: when Debian 14 releases, all nine silently retarget to a suite the image does not use — exactly the mechanism that produced this bug when trixie replaced bookworm.

Note also that the broken `{{#if release }}` construct was **copied from Renovate's own [deb datasource docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/datasource/deb/)**, which document only `suite`, `components` and `binaryArch` — there is no `release` parameter — yet ship that exact example. Recorded for context; not filing upstream for now.

Fixed by **#531**.

### 2. Notification — `mode=silent` suppressed the alarm

**The original claim that `no-result` is "logged at debug level only" is wrong.** Renovate already surfaces lookup failures properly:

- `lookup/index.ts` pushes the failure onto `dep.warnings`
- `errors-warnings.ts` aggregates them and calls **`logger.warn(…, 'Package lookup failures')`** — WARN, not debug
- `getDepWarningsDashboard()` renders "⚠️ Renovate failed to look up the following dependencies: … Files affected: …"
- `dependency-dashboard.ts` writes that into the Dependency Dashboard issue

The only suppression gate is `suppressNotifications: ['dependencyLookupWarnings']`, which this repo does **not** set. So the alarm existed and was unmuted.

It never arrived because the repository runs with **`mode=silent`**. From the job log, verbatim:

```
Repository is running with mode=silent and will not make Issues or PRs by default
Dependency Dashboard issue is not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
Config migration issues are not created, updated or closed when mode=silent
Branch renovate/debian-13.6-slim creation is disabled because mode=silent
Branch renovate/mcr.microsoft.com-windows-servercore-ltsc2025 creation is disabled because mode=silent
```

The lookup failure **did** fire in that run. Silent mode discarded the delivery. This is why Dependency Dashboard #8 has not been rewritten since 2026-07-12 (its body still lists workflow files that no longer exist, and `debian 13.2-slim` while `main` is at 13.6) even though Renovate kept running.

**This is still on, and its blast radius is wider than the alarm:** the same run withheld **two real updates** — `debian 13.6-slim` and `windows/servercore:ltsc2025`. Renovate computed them and declined to open branches.

`mode` is set outside the repository — it is absent from `.github/renovate.json` and from the log's `File`/`CLI`/`Env` config objects, so it comes from Mend's per-repository settings. That is why no amount of reading the repo could find it.

## Decision: stay on openjdk-17

The original plan raised migrating to trixie's `openjdk-21` to delete the bookworm special case. **Researched and decided against.** Flutter publishes a *floor*, not a recommendation:

| Source (Flutter 3.44.9) | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `gradle_utils.dart` `errorJavaMinVersionAndroid` / `warnJavaMinVersionAndroid` | 17 | Floor; errors below, no upper bound |
| `DependencyVersionChecker.kt` `warnJavaVersion` / `errorJavaVersion` | 17 | Same floor, checked downward only |
| **`flutter create` template** `compileOptions.sourceCompatibility` | **17** | **What a real Flutter app declares** |
| `DEPS` → `flutter/java/openjdk` | 21 | Flutter's *engine CI* JDK — "required for running the formatter" |

The `DEPS` pin to 21 is Flutter's own build tooling, not a user-facing recommendation. `flutter create` — the closest thing to an official position — scaffolds **17**. Migrating would be a deliberate divergence from upstream with no source to justify it.

For the record, it would not have removed the hazard anyway: `openjdk-21-jdk-headless` carries the identical strict sibling `Depends: openjdk-21-jre-headless (= 21.0.11+10-1~deb13u2)`.

**Consequence:** Debian 12 bookworm stays permanently, which makes #531's cross-suite packageRule a permanent requirement rather than a stopgap.

## Goal

Renovate's candidate version for an apt pin should equal the version apt would actually install, for every pin — and when that breaks, it should be **visible without anyone reading a job log**.

1. No pin resolves against a suite the image does not enable.
2. Every pin is resolved against the full set of suites the image *does* enable — base, `-updates` and `-security`.
3. A pin that stops resolving is reported where it will be seen.
4. No config field exists that looks like it steers behaviour but doesn't.
5. The Java version the image ships is derived from Flutter, not hand-maintained or measured after the fact.

## Plan

**1. Fix the resolution (#531 — in review)**

`registryUrlTemplate` renders one URL and the deb datasource takes one suite per URL, but apt's candidate is the maximum across every enabled suite. The mechanism cannot express what correctness requires, so it is removed rather than repaired.

- [x] Move suite selection to `packageRules`, whose `registryUrls` is a list; `registryStrategy: "merge"` aggregates releases across suites, matching apt's semantics
- [x] Each entry mirrors one stanza of the image's real apt sources
- [x] Use Debian codenames, not `stable`/`oldstable`, so a new Debian release cannot silently retarget the pins
- [x] **Breaking:** drop `suite=` from the `# renovate:` annotations
- [ ] Record the openjdk-21 decision above and the upstream-docs origin of the typo in the PR body
- [ ] Confirm on the next Renovate run that `getReleases` lists more than one deb `registryUrl` and no `no-result` warning appears — **blocked until `mode=silent` is off**

**2. Restore the alarm — set `mode: "full"`**

Repo config overrides what the app sets globally ([renovatebot/renovate#26724](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/issues/26724)), so this belongs in the repository rather than only the portal — a portal-only toggle is invisible to code review and re-settable without a commit.

- [ ] Add `"mode": "full"` to `.github/renovate.json`, pushed on a `renovate/reconfigure` branch so Renovate validates it
- [ ] Verify on the next job log that it reports `mode=full`; if it still reports `silent`, Mend is forcing the value and the portal is the only lever
- [ ] Confirm Dependency Dashboard #8 is rewritten and the two withheld updates appear

**3. Derive the Java version from Flutter**

`config/version.json`'s `android.java.version` is currently derived **backwards** — a weekly job runs `script/java_version.sh` inside the *previously published* image. It therefore describes the last build, lags a cycle by construction, and feeds nothing user-visible. Editing it changes nothing about what is installed.

The repo already has the right pattern: `script/updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts` is appended to a real `flutter create` app and interrogates the live toolchain for `gradle`, `buildTools`, `ndk` and `platforms`.

- [ ] Extend that task to read `compileOptions.sourceCompatibility` (same dual-DSL fallback as `buildToolsVersion`, failing loudly if absent)
- [ ] Delete `script/java_version.sh` and the backwards derivation step in `update-version.yml`
- [ ] Wire `JAVA_HOME` (`android.Dockerfile:140`) — currently hand-typed and guarded by nothing
- [ ] Decide whether the Dockerfile pin *follows* the derived value or *gates* on it. The major version is welded into the ARG name (`OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION`), so a future 17→21 move is a rename plus a suite change, not a value bump. Leaning: derive `version.json`, fail CI loudly on divergence, keep the migration a deliberate human change
- [ ] Consider publishing the Java version in `readme.md`, which currently never mentions it

**4. Convention for Renovate config changes**

Renovate validates a branch matching `{{branchPrefix}}reconfigure` and posts a status to it ([docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/config-validation/)) — but only on its next scheduled run, so it is a convention, not a gate.

- [ ] Record a short rule in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`: changes to `.github/renovate.json` go on a `renovate/reconfigure` branch
- [ ] Optional hard gate: `script/renovate_validate.sh` in `build.yml` filtered to `paths: ['.github/renovate.json']`. The script exists and is currently invoked by **nothing** — its only "call sites" are checkboxes in change documents

## Deliberately not doing

- **A network dry-run CI guard.** The original plan proposed asserting every deb pin resolves. It would detect only the one seam that is already loud twice over (the dashboard warning and the build failing), it would miss the config-vs-config seams where both real bugs actually were, and — decisively — a guard reporting through Renovate's own channels would have been silenced by `mode=silent` too.
- **An upstream PR to renovatebot/renovate** for the `{{#if release }}` docs example. Noted in #531 instead.

## References

- #529 — hand-fixed the broken build (merged)
- #531 — fixes the Renovate resolution (in review)
- #486 / #488 — the previous silent-staleness bug in this capability
- `openspec/changes/renovate-deb-registry-sets/` — #531's proposal, design and spec delta
- `openspec/changes/loud-deb-pin-resolution/research.md` — full investigation, findings F1–F9 with citations

<details>
<summary>Original issue text (2026-08-07), superseded above</summary>

The original text claimed the `no-result` was "logged at **debug** level only" and that no PR, dashboard entry, or warning was produced. That is incorrect — Renovate emits it at WARN and renders it on the Dependency Dashboard; `mode=silent` suppressed the delivery.

It also proposed, as a maintainer decision, migrating openjdk-17 → openjdk-21 to delete `config/debian_12_bookworm.sources` and the cross-suite pin. That was researched and decided against; see "Decision: stay on openjdk-17".

The remaining original content — the failure, the resolution root cause, and the impact of the suite misconfiguration — is preserved above.

</details>
EOF

Two root causes now, stated as independent:

```

Three things float free: the manifest is measured from the *previous* image, and `JAVA_HOME` and the pin are hand-typed with nothing checking them against each other.

Before I design the wiring, one decision shapes everything downstream — the open question from the research:

**Does the Dockerfile pin *follow* the derived value, or merely *gate* on it?**

- **Gate** — derive `version.json` from Flutter; CI fails loudly if the shipped JDK major diverges. The 17→21 move stays a deliberate human change (it's a rename + suite change, since the major is welded into the ARG name).
- **Follow** — the pin itself is regenerated from the derived value. Fully automatic, but a Flutter template bump would try to rewrite the ARG name and switch Debian suites on its own.

I lean **gate** — the extraction's job is to tell you Flutter moved, not to perform a suite migration unattended. Do you want me to explore the design under that assumption, or do you want follow?

content.text:
The full path is now visible. Java following the derived value works — with one structural difference that has to be designed around.

## The pattern Java joins

```
config/version.json
      │
      ▼  setEnvironmentVariables.js       (core.exportVariable)
  ANDROID_NDK_VERSION, CMAKE_VERSION, …
      │
      ▼  build.yml build-args
  android_ndk_version=…, cmake_version=…
      │
      ▼  android.Dockerfile
  ARG android_ndk_version                 ← no default, injected
```

Note the convention: manifest-fed args are **lowercase with no default** (`android_ndk_version`, `cmake_version`, `flutter_version`). Renovate-fed apt pins are **UPPERCASE with a literal default** (`CURL_VERSION="8.14.1-2+deb13u4"`). Two different mechanisms, cleanly separated by naming.

## The complication

Java is the only value that is **both**. The other manifest args are SDK component versions passed to `sdkmanager` — free-form strings. The Java pin is an **apt package version**, which means two facts, not one:

| Fact | Example | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Java **major** | `17` | Flutter (derived) |
| Debian **package version** | `17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1` | Renovate |
| Package **name** | `openjdk-17-jdk-headless` | contains the major |
| **Suite** | bookworm | determined by the major |

So "follow the derived value" can't mean a single arg. The major and the patch version have different sources and different update cadences.

## Design that fits

Split them — major from the manifest, patch from Renovate:

```dockerfile
ARG android_java_version                                  # from version.json (derived)
# renovate: depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless
ARG OPENJDK_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1"    # Renovate-owned

ENV JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/java-${android_java_version}-openjdk-amd64"

RUN apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    "openjdk-${android_java_version}-jdk-headless=$OPENJDK_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION" \
```

Which gives you:
- `JAVA_HOME` **follows** the derived value — the hand-typed `17` is gone.
- The install line **follows** it too — the package name is composed, not hardcoded.
- The ARG name loses its welded `17`, so a Flutter bump to 21 is a value change, not a rename.
- Renovate still owns the patch version, unchanged.

And it makes the divergence **structurally impossible to ship silently**: if Flutter moves to 21 while the pin still says `17.0.20+…`, the build fails at `apt-get install openjdk-21-jdk-headless=17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1` — no version match. Loud, at build time, exactly where the original bug surfaced.

## The one thing that does *not* follow automatically

The **suite**. A move to 21 means dropping bookworm and its `packageRule` — Renovate can't do that, and neither can a build arg. That step stays human.

So: `JAVA_HOME` and the package name follow automatically; the suite migration is a deliberate change that the build *forces* you to make rather than letting you drift.

Two things I'd want to confirm before writing this up as a design:

1. **`ENV` can't reference `ARG` across stages** — the existing TODOs at `android.Dockerfile:136-138` cite [moby/moby#29110](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/29110). I need to verify `ENV JAVA_HOME="…${android_java_version}…"` actually interpolates in the same stage where the ARG is declared. I believe it does, but it's the load-bearing assumption.
2. **`config/android.cue` and `test/android.yml`** already assert the Java major from the manifest — that guard keeps working unchanged and becomes the runtime confirmation.

Want me to verify the ARG-in-ENV interpolation and then write this into the research file as the design?

Verified end-to-end: the interpolated value is baked into the image config and present at runtime.

## Your concern was right in general, wrong for this case

`ENV` **can** reference `ARG` — but only within the same build stage. That distinction is exactly what the existing TODOs are about:

```dockerfile
# TODO: Get JAVA_HOME dinamically from a JDK binary
# TODO: Use `dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(which javac)))` after ...
# TODO: https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/29110
```

[moby#29110](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/29110) is about something different — wanting `ENV` to capture the **output of a shell command** (`ENV JAVA_HOME=$(dirname ...)`). That's still unsupported. But substituting a build arg is plain variable interpolation and has always worked.

So the blocker in those TODOs doesn't apply here. We're not asking Docker to run a command — we're passing a value we already have.

## What this means for the design

Both hand-typed sites can follow the derived value, in the same stage where the ARG is declared:

```dockerfile
ARG android_java_version
ENV ANDROID_HOME="$SDK_ROOT/android-sdk" \
    JAVA_HOME="/usr/lib/jvm/java-${android_java_version}-openjdk-amd64"

# renovate: suite=bookworm depName=openjdk-17-jdk-headless
ARG OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION="17.0.20+8-1~deb12u1"

RUN apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    "openjdk-${android_java_version}-jdk-headless=$OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION" \
```

One ordering constraint: `ARG android_java_version` currently sits at line 176, *after* the `ENV` at 139-140. It has to move above the `ENV` block. That's a small reshuffle, not a restructure.

Keeping everything 17-specific as-is for now, per your call — the Renovate annotation, the ARG name, the bookworm suite. The only change is that `JAVA_HOME` and the package name stop being independently hand-typed and start deriving from the manifest.

## Full chain, 17 only

```
flutter create app  ──▶ compileOptions.sourceCompatibility = 17
        │                (updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts, extended)
        ▼
config/version.json  android.java.version = 17
        │
        ▼ setEnvironmentVariables.js → ANDROID_JAVA_VERSION
        │
        ▼ build.yml build-args → android_java_version=17
        │
        ├──▶ ENV JAVA_HOME=…/java-17-openjdk-amd64
        └──▶ apt-get install openjdk-17-jdk-headless=$OPENJDK_17_JDK_HEADLESS_VERSION
                                     ▲
                                     └── Renovate still owns the patch version
```

Deleted along the way: `script/java_version.sh` and the backwards derivation step in `update-version.yml:296-303`.

Three things to note before I write this up:

1. **`test/android.yml` keeps working unchanged** — it already asserts the Java major from the manifest via `config/android.cue`, so it becomes the runtime confirmation that the chain is correct.
2. **The web target** — `build.yml:156-157` says android build-args are inert for it, so adding one to the shared block is safe.
3. **Both build-arg blocks** need the new arg (lines 158-164 and 180-186; the second is the fork path).

I have the complete picture. Here is the audit.

---

# Version-Propagation Audit

## Bottom line

**The wiring is not near-minimal, but the bulk of it is necessary.** The core design — one JSON manifest, CUE-validated, read by one JS shim into build-args — is sound and I would not replace it. The incidental complexity is concentrated in four places: **a live bug that silently ships the wrong build-tools version to every release**, a value derived backwards from the previously-built image, two parallel pin mechanisms (JSON vs. Dockerfile ARG), and 8 dead scripts. Removing those is roughly **-1 script, -2 workflow lines, -8 files, and one production defect** without touching the architecture.

## 🔴 Critical: `android_build_tools_version` is overridden to `30.0.3` in every release

This is a real, shipping bug, not a design smell.

- `release.yml:42` sets job-level `env: ANDROID_BUILD_TOOLS_VERSION: 30.0.3`
- `release.yml:53-62` then runs `setEnvironmentVariables.js`, which `core.exportVariable`s the same name from `version.json` (`36.0.0`)
- **`core.exportVariable` writes to `$GITHUB_ENV`, but a job-level `env:` key takes precedence over `$GITHUB_ENV` for the rest of the job.** The job-level literal wins.
- `release.yml:117` therefore passes `android_build_tools_version=30.0.3` to the build.

Same pattern at `ci.yml:29` + `ci.yml:87`. `build.yml` has **no** such override (`build.yml:161`), so it correctly passes `36.0.0`.

Consequence: PR builds install build-tools `36.0.0`; released images install `30.0.3`. `test/android.yml:22-27` asserts `36.0.0`, and it passes — because `build.yml`/`ci.yml` structure-tests are run against differently-built images than `release.yml` publishes. `ci.yml:93` does test the `30.0.3` image against `test/android.yml`… which expects `36.0.0`. Worth confirming against a published image, but the code path is unambiguous.

**Fix: delete `release.yml:42` and `ci.yml:29`.** Two lines. This is the single highest-value change in the audit.

## Trace table

Hops = distinct mechanisms between upstream truth and the running image.

| Value | Origin | Fetched at | Lands | Reaches image | Validated by | Updated by | Hops |

| android.platforms | live Gradle read (`flutter.targetSdkVersion`) | `updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts:11-14` | version.json + ARG | build-arg → `sdkmanager` (`android.Dockerfile:210`) | none (no test asserts) | update-version.yml:286-290 | 5 |
| android.buildTools | live AGP extension read | `updateAndroidVersions.gradle.kts:22-28` | version.json + ARG | build-arg (`android.Dockerfile:207`) — **but overridden, see above** | test/android.yml:22-27 | update-version.yml | 5 |
